docs.text: Role: E10 cross-theme BNPL merchant-network and consumer-credit owner Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Updated: 2026-07-13; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Affirm places merchant distribution, consumer installments, and pay-over-time products inside one payment-network framework. Core revenue comes from merchant, transaction/network, and consumer-credit economics rather than a standalone AI revenue line.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: AFRM belongs to the E10 cross-theme fintech portfolio, not an AI or data-center supply spine. It owns the BNPL merchant-network and consumer-credit role. It does not absorb SOFI's digital-bank and lending platform, HOOD's retail-brokerage and crypto entry point, or a generic application or infrastructure-owner role.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: The current local issuer packet provides no standalone AI/ML monetization proof. If AI/ML supports underwriting, fraud, servicing, or productivity, value still has to appear in approval quality, loss performance, merchant conversion, cost, or network economics. This page does not place it in the realized revenue bridge before direct evidence exists.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Official IR materials and the FY2026 Q2 results define Affirm as a payment network connecting consumers and merchants.
  • The local packet treats Active Consumers and GMV as operating metrics and places merchant-growth tools and pay-over-time products in one framework. Those are network and credit anchors, not AI revenue.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Company framing emphasizes the payment network and pay-over-time products that help consumers and merchants grow.
  • The local packet contains no management metric that can be promoted into standalone AI monetization.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• Better risk decisioning, fraud control, or servicing could improve approvals, losses, and merchant economics.
  • That inference can be upgraded only when direct issuer evidence ties model capability to verifiable operating results.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AI/ML has created separately trackable revenue, profit, or paid attach.
  • Broad GMV, Active Consumer, or merchant growth is directly attributable to AI.
  • AFRM should absorb SOFI, HOOD, or a wider application or infrastructure role.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Deteriorating credit losses, funding costs, or capital-market availability would weaken network economics.
  • If merchant and consumer growth does not become healthy take rate and credit performance, scale alone is not enough.
  • If direct model-to-outcome evidence remains absent, AI/ML stays an unproven support mechanism.

docs.text: Active / Market-found BNPL merchant-network and consumer-credit owner. Current action lives in Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger.

docs.title: AMD — Advanced Micro Devices
docs.text:
Role: spine 2 CPU host compute + accelerator platform Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-04

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for AMD; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: AMD earns from EPYC server CPUs, Instinct accelerators, client chips, and embedded products. Its AI value is a combined CPU-host and GPU-accelerator platform. Data Center is already financial, while competitiveness still depends on ROCm, product cadence, customer deployment, and supply scaling.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: AMD primary-owns CPU/host and accelerator nodes in Semiconductors and Foundational Compute. It relies on external foundry, advanced packaging, and HBM, so wafer/package realization remains in Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials and physical memory in Memory, Storage, and In-System Data Movement.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: EPYC and Instinct/Helios purchases for training, inference, and agents become processor/accelerator revenue. ROCm, system qualification, and supply determine adoption. Data-center mix, gross margin, FCF, and repeat deployment—not roadmap alone—measure the economics.

docs.title: 2026-08-04 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2026 revenue was USD 11.536B, up 50% year over year. Data Center revenue was USD 6.718B, up 107%, and non-GAAP EPS was USD 1.66.
  • Management guided Q3 revenue to about USD 13.0B ± 0.3B and non-GAAP gross margin to about 56%; shipment, customer, and product-mix evidence still determine how much of the reported growth belongs to the accelerator bridge.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2026 revenue was USD 10.253B, up 38%.
  • Data Center revenue was USD 5.775B, up 57%; AMD called it the main driver of revenue and earnings growth.
  • Q1 FCF was a record USD 2.566B.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • The prior Q2 revenue guidance, given after Q1, was about USD 11.2B ± 0.3B, with non-GAAP gross margin near 56%; Q2 actual results released on 2026-08-04 supersede that dated forecast. Management says MI450/Helios engagement and the large-deployment pipeline exceed initial expectations, with server growth accelerating as supply scales. Orders, shipments, and mix still need proof.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: A CPU+GPU portfolio can increase platform attach and system bargaining power beyond one accelerator SKU.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Not all Data Center growth is Instinct. Roadmap/pipeline is not backlog or high-margin revenue, and ROCm, customer concentration, and supply constraints remain material.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Data Center growth or gross margin repeatedly misses the roadmap and peers.
  • MI-series deployments fail to produce repeat customers, software adoption, or scale revenue.
  • EPYC share gains stall and CPU/accelerator synergy does not show up.
  • Foundry, package, HBM, or export limits block delivery.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: AMD is a Core / Market-found compute platform and the main financial accelerator/CPU benchmark after NVIDIA; the old “challenger” label is incomplete.

docs.title: AMKR — Amkor
docs.text: Last updated: 2026-08-19 CEST

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
• Structural status: context
  • Current role: Market-found, benchmark-only
  • Primary lane: spine 5 outsourced packaging / test benchmark
  • Boundary: recognizes its place in advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and SiP; does not treat it as an active selection or recast it as a chip-design or pure data-center revenue name
  • Action pointer: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: Business and lane position
docs.text: Amkor is defined in the issuer raw as a global outsourced semiconductor packaging and test leader, with advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package offerings explicitly aimed at end markets including data centers and AI. Its lane-5 position is real, but it is better used as a packaging-and-test platform benchmark than as a high-purity AI focus name.

docs.title: AI to revenue
docs.text: The AI transmission is more direct than for many OSATs, but the revenue base is still mixed. In 2025, net sales were $6.708 billion, with packaging services at 89% and test services at 11%; computing represented 20% of end-market mix while communications represented 46%. The company also disclosed $5.556 billion of advanced products revenue in 2025, and management said 2025 delivered record Advanced packaging and Computing revenue. That is enough to say AI / data-center demand has entered revenue, but not enough to treat the company as a pure AI packaging exposure.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The company defines itself as a leading OSAT, with advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package capabilities.
  • In 2025, net sales were $6.708 billion; packaging services were 89%, test services were 11%, and computing represented 20% of end-market mix.
  • In 2025, one customer represented 29.8% of total net sales, a second customer represented 11.1%, and the top ten customers represented 72%.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management said 2025 delivered record Advanced packaging and Computing revenue and that the company is accelerating investment for the next wave of advanced-packaging growth.
  • The 2026 capital-expenditure plan of about $2.5 billion to $3.0 billion, Arizona expansion, and related growth plans remain forward-looking statements.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: • As foundries, fabless companies, and IDMs continue outsourcing heterogeneous integration, wafer-level processing, and package test, Amkor should benefit as a back-end manufacturing platform.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AI revenue share.
  • Advanced packaging is already large enough to outweigh mobile, automotive, and broader end-market cyclicality.
  • The company should be upgraded from benchmark-only to active selection.

docs.title: 2026-08-19 issuer-primary closure correction
docs.text:
• CLOSED — named Arizona linkage: Amkor issuer-primary materials now name the Apple–TSMC Arizona–Amkor chain, the TSMC 10-year advanced-packaging/test procurement framework, and NVIDIA's $1.5B multi-year advanced-packaging/development agreement supporting Arizona capacity.
  • PARTIAL — Arizona economics: specific fab/capacity allocation, volume, price, cancellation/refund, revenue-recognition, and margin terms remain undisclosed. The 2026-07-28 10-Q's unnamed customer advance must not be legally or accounting-wise merged with the named NVIDIA agreement.
  • BLOCKED-PUBLIC-DISCLOSURE — HBM monetization: the reviewed issuer filing/deck set does not disclose auditable HBM revenue, order/backlog, or margin; this terminal public-disclosure state is not a claim that no HBM activity occurred. Historical strict-FCF measurement is CLOSED and remains USD -306.852M; no realized capex-to-cash recovery is shown.
  • CLOSED — no promotion: selected current-action SOT=none; numeric-zone authority=NO; AMKR remains context / benchmark-only and large position=NO.

docs.title: Company kill criteria
docs.text:
• Advanced packaging / computing stops being a growth focus or stops converting into revenue realization.
  • Customer concentration worsens further without broader customer expansion.
  • The page drifts back into treating Amkor as a pure AI packaging winner while ignoring its multi-end-market and customer-concentration profile.

docs.title: AMZN — Amazon
docs.text: Role: spine 1 hyperscale demand / capacity benchmark; AWS is the main AI mechanism Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-04-29; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Amazon's earnings span AWS, retail/logistics, advertising, and subscriptions. For AI, AWS matters most: customers pay for compute, storage, databases, Bedrock, and custom-silicon capacity. Amazon as a whole is not a pure AI entity, so this page treats it as a hyperscale-demand and capital-intensity benchmark.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: AWS buys and operates capacity in Cloud and Compute Demand and influences compute mix through Trainium, Graviton, and Nitro. Amazon resembles other merchant clouds, but retail, advertising, and logistics make consolidated earnings different from AI demand alone.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AWS compute and Bedrock/agent usage generate consumption revenue. Custom silicon may lower unit cost and expand capacity. Large commitments improve visibility, but only deployment, utilization, and service mix turn them into AWS revenue, operating income, and cash.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2026 AWS sales were USD 37.6B, up 28%; AWS operating income was USD 14.2B.
  • The chips business exceeded a USD 20B annual revenue run rate with triple-digit growth.
  • TTM operating cash flow was USD 148.5B, but AI property/equipment purchases helped reduce TTM FCF to USD 1.2B.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • Amazon disclosed that OpenAI committed to about 2GW of Trainium capacity beginning in 2027 and Anthropic will use up to 5GW of current/future Trainium capacity; a disclosed commitment is not deployed capacity or recognized revenue.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Trainium, Graviton, Bedrock, and merchant-cloud scale can improve price/performance and model choice, supporting AWS share in AI workloads.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Capacity commitments are not near-term revenue, full utilization, or high margin. Not all Amazon capex is AI, and custom-silicon growth does not guarantee consolidated FCF improvement.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: AWS is a genuine AI-infrastructure profit pool, but Amazon shareholder returns still depend on retail efficiency, advertising, logistics, and capex. It is a demand benchmark, not a physical bottleneck owner or undiscovered pure-play.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AWS growth or operating margin slows while capacity keeps expanding.
  • AI property/equipment spend depresses FCF without sufficient utilization and pricing.
  • GPU, power, network, or customer concentration delays deployment or weakens pricing.
  • Hyperscaler, neo-cloud, and model-platform competition limits Bedrock/Trainium adoption.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: AMZN is a Context / Market-found hyperscale-demand benchmark focused on AWS mechanisms and cash-conversion boundaries.

docs.title: ANET — Arista Networks
docs.text:
Role: spine-4 networking and Ethernet-fabric platform benchmark Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Updated: 2026-09-09

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects ANET and Nokia Current Live Execution Zones as ANET's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Arista sells a full networking and Ethernet-fabric platform for AI, data-center, campus, and routing environments. It is the benchmark for the system-platform layer, not a connectivity semiconductor or optics-only component supplier.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: ANET belongs to the networking and fabric-platform node in spine 4 AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI. It owns switching, routing, fabric OS, and system-level network control. It does not absorb CRDO/ALAB link-level semiconductors, reduce itself to optics/DCI components, or own spine-6 EMS/NPI and server manufacturing.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI-cluster expansion requires more Ethernet switching, routing, and fabric control, and Arista monetizes through platform hardware, software, and related services. Q1 FY2026 company revenue growth proves platform demand converted into reported results, but there is no separate AI revenue split, so broad company revenue is not AI-specific revenue.

docs.title: 2026-08-04 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2026 revenue was USD 3.036B, up 37.7% year over year. GAAP operating margin was 45.4% and non-GAAP operating margin was 49.9%.
  • The issuer continued to frame 1.6T networking as part of the platform transition; it did not disclose an AI-only revenue split.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text: • Q1 FY2026 revenue was USD 2.709B, up 35.1% year over year.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The issuer release positions Arista as a data-driven client-to-cloud networking platform for AI, data-center, campus, and routing environments. That framing supports system-platform placement rather than a component-only role.
  • Management says Arista is well positioned at the confluence of secure client-to-campus-to-cloud and AI networking.
  • That statement supports product and market positioning, not an AI-specific revenue or share disclosure.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If Ethernet keeps carrying AI scale-out and data-center network upgrades, ANET can expand revenue through switching/routing platforms, EOS, and cluster-network control.
  • That value capture still requires revenue, margin, customer-mix, and platform-adoption proof rather than a direct extrapolation from AI-networking TAM.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The dollar amount of Q1 growth attributable only to AI.
  • Long-run AI-Ethernet share versus proprietary or custom fabrics is already locked in.
  • ANET should absorb connectivity-semiconductor, optical-component, DCI-transport, or systems-manufacturing ownership.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If the AI-networking narrative strengthens while company growth, margin, or platform adoption fails to follow, the benchmark conclusion should be downgraded.
  • If proprietary or custom fabrics durably weaken Ethernet in target deployments, ANET's AI spillover will be lower than expected.
  • If later sources prove only broad campus/routing recovery without a continuing AI/data-center link, this page should narrow its AI framing.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Context / Market-found networking and Ethernet-fabric platform benchmark. It remains a system-platform reference rather than a link-component owner.

docs.title: APO — Apollo Global Management
docs.text:
Last updated: 2026-09-09 CEST

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for APO; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text:
• Structural status: context
  • Current role: Market-found
  • Primary lane: Phase 5 E10 cross-theme portfolio; alternative-asset plus retirement-services / permanent-capital benchmark
  • Boundary: APO's durable role is the benchmark for alternative asset management plus retirement-services and permanent-capital structure, centered on asset management, Athene, and the origination engine; it is not a standalone AI revenue name and it does not absorb bank, payments, application-owner, or physical-infrastructure-owner roles

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: In the local issuer packet, APO is defined as an alternative-asset platform organized around yield, hybrid, and equity, with Athene providing retirement services and permanent capital. Its E10 role is not to join the AI / data-center supply chain, but to benchmark how long-duration capital, insurance liabilities, and private-financing capacity absorb macro and AI-capex spillover.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: For APO, AI is at most an indirect bridge through financing, asset allocation, and internal efficiency. If AI buildout increases demand for private credit, hybrid capital, asset-backed financing, industrial origination, or retirement-capital allocation into alternative yield assets, APO can benefit through fee-related earnings, spread-related earnings, and Athene's permanent-capital structure. But the current local issuer packet does not disclose AI as a separate reporting segment, so broad AUM, origination, or inflow actuals cannot be treated as direct AI proof.

docs.title: 2026-08-04 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 net income was USD 1.336B, fee-related earnings were USD 785M, and assets under management were USD 1.05T.
  • These are operating and balance-sheet facts for the alternative-asset platform; the local issuer capture still does not disclose AI as a distinct revenue line.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The company disclosed more than $300 billion of origination activity and more than $225 billion of inflows in 2025, driving record fee-related earnings and spread-related earnings.
  • As of 2025-12-31, AUM was approximately $938 billion; the local IR packet also organizes the platform around yield, hybrid, and equity and explicitly identifies the retirement-services business and Athene.
  • The local IR packet shows formal disclosure entry points for first-quarter 2026 earnings and the February 2026 investor presentation.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management describes Apollo as helping build the next generation of financial services through financing the industrial renaissance, advancing retirement solutions, and enabling broader buyer access to private markets.
  • Retirement services, Athene, and the origination engine are repeated public operating anchors, but the current local packet does not break AI out as a revenue line.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI buildout keeps increasing demand for private financing, asset-backed lending, hybrid capital, and retirement allocation into alternative assets, APO should benefit through its existing alternative-asset and permanent-capital machine.
  • That benefit comes first from the capital-source and asset-deployment structure rather than from a separately named AI product revenue stream.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AI has become a separately trackable revenue or profit disclosure.
  • Broad AUM, origination, inflows, or spread-related earnings are enough on their own to prove an independent AI contribution.
  • APO should absorb the roles of large banks, payment networks, physical-infrastructure owners, or application owners.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later local issuer / SEC packets cannot keep the permanent-capital and retirement-services role anchored in reported disclosure, this page should remain benchmark-level context rather than being promoted.
  • If the page turns broad origination, AUM, or retirement growth into AI monetization proof, it should revert to the stricter indirect-bridge framing.
  • If the role drifts into bank, payments, E7 / E8 physical-buildout ownership, or application-layer ownership, the boundary is wrong.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Context / Market-found alternative-asset, retirement-services, and permanent-capital benchmark. E10 keeps only the cross-theme capital-structure role.

docs.title: ARM — Arm Holdings
docs.text: Role: spine 2 architecture/IP benchmark Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-06-05; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Arm earns CPU architecture/IP license fees and downstream royalties; it does not manufacture chips. Neoverse, CSS, and Total Design expose it to cloud, custom silicon, and AI/HPC, but AI-server growth does not automatically become Arm server share, royalties, or cash.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: ARM is the architecture/IP node in Semiconductors and Foundational Compute. Customers and foundries complete chip design and manufacturing; realization belongs to Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. Arm economics depend on license, royalty, customer shipment, and contract terms rather than x86 CPU sales or custom-XPU programs.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Customer adoption of Arm IP for CPUs, accelerator companions, or custom silicon first creates license economics; production shipments later create royalties. AI/cloud adoption matters only through design wins, volume, royalty rate, and product cycles.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The FY2026 20-F filed May 2026 maintains Arm's CPU-IP, Neoverse, CSS/Total Design, and cloud/AI/HPC infrastructure positioning.
  • Arm's model is license plus royalty, not chip manufacturing or data-center capacity sales.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Arm presents Neoverse/CSS/Total Design as a base for hyperscaler, sovereign-AI, and custom-silicon expansion; this is product/strategy positioning, not customer-level revenue attribution.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: More custom-silicon designs and architectural diversity may expand the addressable license and royalty pool.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: AMD's Q1 FY2026 Data Center/EPYC growth shows server CPU wallet does not flow automatically to Arm. AI capex does not prove Arm share, royalty rate, or a specific design win.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Neoverse/CSS adoption fails to become visible license/royalty growth.
  • x86 or another architecture maintains superior server/AI-host performance or TCO.
  • Customer self-design, disputes, concentration, or royalty terms weaken economics.
  • Market expectations outgrow actual royalty and cash growth for an extended period.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: ARM is a Context / Market-found architecture/IP benchmark, not an accelerator or foundry owner.

docs.title: ASX — ASE Technology
docs.text: Last updated: 2026-07-13 CEST

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
• Structural status: context
  • Current role: Market-found, benchmark-only
  • Primary lane: spine 5 OSAT / packaging / test benchmark
  • Boundary: recognizes ATM, testing, and packaging exposure; does not treat ASE as an active selection, and does not recast its EMS / system-manufacturing exposure as a pure AI packaging story
  • Action pointer: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: Business and lane position
docs.text: The issuer raw spans both semiconductor assembly and testing services and EMS. ASE is genuinely in the back-end manufacturing chain for AI chips, but the consolidated mix is still heavily shaped by EMS and broader end-market cycles. This page therefore keeps ASE as a benchmark for advanced-packaging and test conditions rather than a primary selection.

docs.title: AI to revenue
docs.text: The AI transmission is real but diluted. In 2024 packaging / testing revenue, communications, computing, and consumer electronics / industrial / automotive / other represented about 50.9%, 18.1%, and 31.0%, respectively. In EMS, computing was only about 10.1%. In 4Q25, packaging, testing, and EMS accounted for about 49%, 12%, and 38% of total revenue. That means AI and advanced packaging can improve ATM, but not enough to rewrite the full company as a high-purity AI OSAT name.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The company describes itself as a leading provider of semiconductor assembly and testing services and EMS.
  • In 4Q25, packaging, testing, and EMS represented about 49%, 12%, and 38% of total revenue, and ATM revenue rose 24.2% year over year.
  • In 2024 packaging / testing revenue, computing represented about 18.1%; in EMS revenue, computing represented about 10.1%.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The IR site frames the company’s advanced packaging and system-integration capabilities as a platform for the AI era.
  • Higher AI value capture from advanced packaging and system integration still remains mostly at the self-positioning level in the current raw.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: • If advanced packaging, testing, and outsourced ATM continue to expand, ASE benefits, but that benefit remains diluted by EMS and broader semiconductor cyclicality.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AI revenue share.
  • Advanced packaging is already strong enough to dominate the consolidated margin profile.
  • The company should be upgraded from benchmark-only to active selection.

docs.title: Company kill criteria
docs.text:
• ATM growth no longer distinguishes itself from EMS or the broader cycle.
  • Computing / advanced-packaging disclosures weaken enough that ASE stops serving as a useful back-end-manufacturing benchmark.
  • The page drifts back into treating ASE as a pure server / rack / EMS AI-delivery name.

docs.title: AVGO — Broadcom
docs.text: Role: spine 2 custom accelerator/XPU; AI networking is secondary Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-09-03; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Broadcom earns from custom AI accelerators, switching/SerDes/DSP/networking silicon, other semiconductors, and infrastructure software. AI value capture comes from custom compute and network programs for a few very large customers, so high growth carries high program and concentration risk.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: AVGO primary-owns custom silicon/XPU in Semiconductors and Foundational Compute and secondary-links AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI. Packaging technology is an implementation capability, while foundry/package manufacturing ownership remains in Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Hyperscalers co-design XPU and networking programs with Broadcom. Design wins convert as each generation/rack rolls out. Long programs, complex IP, networking attach, and scale support value, while customer timing, mix, supply, and program continuity determine cash.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q3 FY2026 revenue was USD 29.591B, up 86%; Semiconductor Solutions was USD 20.839B, up 127%, and Infrastructure Software was USD 8.752B, up 29%.
  • AI semiconductor revenue was USD 16.7B, up 221% and about 54% sequentially.
  • GAAP/non-GAAP diluted EPS was USD 2.68/3.32; FCF was USD 13.665B, or 46.2% of revenue, so the beat was not confined to adjusted EPS.
  • An April 2026 8-K disclosed a long-term Google agreement for future TPU generations and networking/other components for next-generation AI racks through as late as 2031.
  • The Q2 10-Q disclosed about USD 164.6B of remaining performance obligations, including a long-term custom-AI-accelerator contract signed during the quarter; about 30% is expected to be recognized over the next 12 months.
  • The same filing disclosed USD 128.110B of purchase commitments, mainly in FY2027/FY2028. This strengthens capacity/supply commitment evidence while increasing demand-timing and execution sensitivity.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Q4 revenue/AI semiconductor guidance is USD 34.8B/21.7B; total-revenue consensus ranged from USD 34.68B to USD 35.05B, making “roughly in line” more robust than a categorical beat or miss. An automated transcript records management's FY2026/27/28 AI-revenue outlook at about USD 58B/115B/230B and FY2028 EPS above USD 30. These are management outlooks, not filed backlog, and still need official-replay or later-filing verification.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Serving both custom compute and networking can increase wallet share and let AVGO benefit from XPU and some GPU clusters, while increasing customer, financing, site-readiness, HBM/substrate, and program-timing risk.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: The Google agreement does not attribute all TPU/AI revenue or prove diversification. The FY2027/28 outlook is neither an order nor perpetual growth evidence; the Q3 10-Q, future customer-financing terms, and actual site/supply conversion remain open.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI semiconductor revenue or program guidance repeatedly misses materially.
  • A large customer redesigns, dual-sources, internalizes, or delays a program.
  • The top five end customers represented about 45% of Q2/H1 revenue, versus about 40% a year earlier, so large-order timing can amplify quarterly volatility.
  • The Q2 10-Q disclosed a backstop on one customer's five-year AI-rack lease obligations with maximum exposure of USD 29B. This is not expected loss, but it makes part of demand financing-assisted and adds contingent-liability risk.
  • Ethernet/optical/network competition weakens attach, share, or margin.
  • Higher XPU/HBM mix is diluting gross margin; the long-range EPS path fails if operating leverage cannot offset it.
  • Software mix masks semiconductor slowdown or cash conversion deteriorates.
  • The June 11 USD 2.5B capped debt tender is liability management, not evidence to upgrade AI demand or action.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
AVGO is the Core / Market-found custom-silicon anchor with secondary AI networking. The 2026-09-03 research posture is “materially stronger operating evidence and no thesis-break evidence, but valuation remains highly dependent on long-range execution”: at USD 363.90 after hours, Q3 annualized FCF implies about 32.5x price/FCF, while management's FY2028 >USD 30 EPS outlook implies below 12.2x if delivered. This is a positive but valuation-dependent research assessment, not a buy/sell/hold or timing signal.

The registry remains none; this page creates no numeric band, buy/sell execution, or sizing authority. Large-position confirmation: NO.

docs.title: AXTI — AXT
docs.text: Updated: 2026-07-13 Industry page: AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI Action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: AXT's core business is compound-semiconductor wafer substrates, especially indium phosphide (InP) wafers. It sells upstream materials into the optical-communications chain, not optical modules or systems equipment.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Its primary role is an InP substrate supplier upstream of the AI optical chain.
  • Its AI relevance comes from demand for InP in high-speed optical transmission and silicon photonics.
  • The company is not a transceiver, switch, or direct hyperscaler-revenue owner.
  • China manufacturing, the Tongmei structure, and export approvals are part of the role boundary, not footnotes.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If AI data-center expansion lifts demand for high-speed optical transmission, that can first appear as higher InP wafer-substrate demand and then flow into AXTI revenue. The current revenue path is still influenced by passive optical networks and China export approvals, not by AI alone.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 revenue was USD 26.9M, and substrate revenue was USD 19.281M, up 74.0% year over year.
  • Management said in issuer-primary materials that the capital raise would support Tongmei InP capacity expansion and R&D related to 6-inch indium phosphide.
  • The 10-Q attributed substrate growth mainly to higher demand for InP wafers used in data-center applications and passive optical networks, together with additional China export approvals.
  • The 2026-04-21 offering raised about USD 550M gross, or about USD 632.5M if fully exercised, mainly for Tongmei capacity expansion, R&D, and working capital.
  • The 2026-06-17 Tongmei / Casela supply agreement covered RMB 173M of 2027 InP wafers and required 50% prepayment plus an 80% minimum purchase threshold.
  • Q1 2026 revenue geography remained highly China-concentrated: China 61%, North America 1%.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management said InP substrates are a key ingredient for the high-speed optical transmission required in AI-focused data centers.
  • Related 2026-06-22 materials framed the expansion path as an aggressive strategic path driven by AI optical data-transmission demand.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• AXTI has moved from former-half-hidden into Market-found because issuer-primary evidence now links InP materials revenue growth to data-center optical demand.
  • It remains indirect exposure: this page is about an optical-materials bottleneck, not a direct hyperscaler optical-revenue owner.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The page does not cleanly isolate the AI-only share of substrate revenue.
  • The page does not prove that an InP supply squeeze has become durable global pricing power.
  • The page also does not prove that U.S. hyperscaler demand is already the dominant driver rather than broader optical demand plus export approvals.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If issuer-primary evidence stops linking InP growth to data-center optical demand, this page's role should be downgraded.
  • If export approvals or Tongmei capacity expansion stop supporting revenue growth, the AI-to-revenue logic should be rewritten.
  • If Casela-like commitments fail to convert into broader repeatable demand, AXTI should stay only an indirect materials exposure.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: active / Market-found; modifier: former-half-hidden. It is now a seen InP-materials name, but it still belongs to indirect materials exposure inside the optical chain.

docs.text: Updated: 2026-07-13 Industry page: Onsite Bridge Power, Storage, and Backup Action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Bloom Energy's core business is fuel-cell-based onsite power systems and related services. It sells fast site power availability, not utility-generation asset ownership.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• It belongs to the Phase 5 E7 onsite / bridge generation segment inside the generation / grid / time-to-power causal lane.
  • The role boundary stops at onsite generation and fast energization around grid connection. It does not extend into site electrical distribution, rack power, cooling, or EPC spine 8.
  • Bloom's fuel-cell systems are an onsite generation mechanism, not a utility-generation owner.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If AI data centers need power sooner because grid connection, campus delivery, or backup timing is constrained, Bloom can turn that time-to-power need into revenue through onsite fuel-cell systems, deployment work, and follow-on service contracts. That path depends on project conversion and customer buying decisions; it is not utility-generation ownership economics.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Local issuer-primary captures already include named counterparties such as Oracle, CoreWeave, and AEP, and those materials directly connect Bloom's power offering to data-center or AI-data-center scenarios.
  • Local SEC and results captures are sufficient to establish Bloom as a fuel-cell power platform selling systems and related services, not as a theme-only mapping.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company frames its fuel-cell systems as fast-deployment onsite power for data-center time-to-power pressure.
  • Company materials place AI-driven load growth and faster power availability in the same narrative.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• Inside Phase 5 E7, Bloom is an active onsite fuel-cell generation name because the product mechanism and customer use case sit inside the time-to-power lane.
  • This page is about fast onsite power availability, not utility-generation ownership and not downstream room-level power or cooling.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The page does not isolate AI-only revenue, AI-only backlog, or AI-only service annuity.
  • The page does not prove that every named announcement has converted into repeatable attributable data-center revenue.
  • The page also does not prove that Bloom has utility-generation-owner economics.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If future issuer-primary or SEC captures stop linking Bloom's systems to data-center time-to-power use cases, this page's role should be downgraded.
  • If named counterparties remain only at the announcement layer and fail to produce repeat deployment, service, or backlog evidence, the AI-to-revenue logic should be rewritten.
  • If the company narrative moves away from fast data-center energization toward a generic energy story, this page should leave Phase 5 E7 mainline tracking.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: active; modifier: Needs-source. Proof gates: 1. Issuer-primary or filing evidence for named deployment, contracted capacity, or delivered scope. 2. Repeatable product, service, backlog, or annuity evidence tied to that scope. 3. Clear proof that the role remains onsite generation rather than utility-generation ownership.

docs.title: BELFB Bel Fuse Class B
docs.text:
Updated: 2026-07-13

Industry page: AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: BELFB is an Active / Market-found power / magnetics / connectivity company with the body-only modifier former-half-hidden. Its exposure spans front-end power, power shelves, circuit protection, connectors, and Ethernet magnetics from the site electrical boundary to the energized rack. It does not own E7 generation, E2 compute silicon, or E6 full systems.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
BELFB's product exposure sits in Networking & Data Centers power conversion, power shelves / racks, circuit protection, magnetics, and connectivity. It is better understood as a component and subsystem supplier benefiting from data-center electrical and interconnect complexity than as an owner of board-level AI power architecture or a full-system vendor.

Its boundaries also need to stay explicit: - It does not own E7 generation / grid / time-to-power and should not be treated as a site-power owner. - It does not own E2 compute silicon, so chip-volume growth cannot be treated as BELFB revenue by default. - It does not own E6 systems integration, so rack, server, switch, or full-platform delivery should not be assigned to BELFB.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
AI clusters raise rack power, networking density, power protection needs, and connectivity complexity at the same time. BELFB monetizes that through more power, magnetic, and connectivity content inside OEM, ODM, server, switch, and data-infrastructure platforms.

That mechanism still needs to stay under issuer-claim discipline: the company already uses language around networking, data infrastructure, datacenter connectivity, and high-performance compute tied to AI-driven investment, but it has not directly disclosed AI revenue, named customers, or data-center order dollars.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• BELFB's SEC and primary captures show the company operating Power Solutions and Protection, Connectivity Solutions, and Magnetic Solutions businesses.
  • The official Networking & Data Centers product page lists AC-DC, DC-DC, power shelves / racks, MagJack ICMs, PoE transformers, chokes / inductors, circuit protection, and related products.
  • The SEC primary capture also shows materially higher FY2025 orders and Q1 FY2026 backlog, including Industrial Technology & Data Solutions backlog growth versus year-end 2025, which means the exposure is already flowing into operating results.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management links Industrial Technology & Data Solutions to networking and data infrastructure demand.
  • Management framing supports datacenter connectivity and high-performance compute tied to AI-driven investment as demand support for relevant products.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI data centers keep increasing rack power and network complexity, BELFB can capture more second-order component revenue across power, magnetics, and connectivity.
  • The benefit is more likely to show up through diversified part-number and subsystem content than through concentrated ownership of a rack-entry power platform like AEIS.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• It is not yet proven that BELFB has a quantifiable AI revenue bucket.
  • It is not yet proven that BELFB has attributable revenue from a named hyperscaler, GPU OEM, AI server OEM, or switch platform.
  • It is not yet proven that data-center or AI order dollars can be cleanly separated from broader segment performance.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later issuer-primary materials stop identifying networking or data-infrastructure demand as a growth support, this page should be downgraded.
  • If the product exposure turns out to be mostly low-value generic parts rather than components pulled by data-center power and interconnect complexity, the core framing should shrink.
  • If later evidence shows the relevant growth is mainly coming from non-data-center end markets rather than datacenter connectivity or rack-power demand, the page needs to be rewritten.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
Active / Market-found; modifier: former-half-hidden. The E8 role is power / magnetics / connectivity from the site electrical boundary to the energized rack, with a hard boundary at not owning E7 generation, E2 compute silicon, or E6 systems.

docs.title: BESI — BE Semiconductor Industries
docs.text: Role: spine-5 hybrid-bonding and advanced-assembly equipment benchmark Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Updated: 2026-08-04; action entry: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Besi supplies advanced-assembly, die-attach, and hybrid-bonding equipment, turning 2.5D/3D advanced-packaging complexity into equipment orders and revenue. It is the bonding/attach benchmark rather than a substrate, inspection, probe/test, or systems-manufacturing owner. Q2 2026 moved hybrid-bonding, photonics, datacenter, and AI power-management demand from technology narrative into reported orders, revenue, and high margins.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: BESI belongs to the bonding, attach, and hybrid-bonding equipment node in spine 5 Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. It owns high-accuracy placement and advanced-interconnect assembly. It does not absorb ONTO/CAMT inspection and metrology, FORM/TER probe and test, TSM/OSAT foundry and package platforms, or spine-6 server/rack manufacturing.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI compute raises 2.5D/3D integration and interconnect-density requirements. Customers buy hybrid-bonding and advanced-assembly equipment that becomes orders, shipments, and revenue. Q2/H1 2026 shows simultaneous expansion in orders, revenue, customer count, and use cases, while the high AI order mix also raises customer-capex and delivery-timing concentration.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q2 revenue was EUR 249.9M, up 35.2% sequentially and 68.7% year over year; orders were EUR 292.9M, up 8.6% sequentially and 128.8% year over year.
  • Q2 gross margin was 65.7%, operating income EUR 108.8M / operating margin 43.5%, and net income EUR 89.0M.
  • H1 revenue was EUR 434.7M, orders EUR 562.6M, and net income EUR 140.6M; LTM orders reached a record EUR 987.6M.
  • Besi estimated AI applications at about 60% of H1 system orders. Hybrid-bonding customers increased from 15 at 2025 year-end to 21; use cases cover logic, memory, co-packaged optics, and consumer. Q2 included two repeat customers and one new hyperscaler.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Q3 revenue guidance calls for 10%-15% sequential growth, gross margin of 63%-65%, and operating expenses flat to up 5%. This is forward guidance.
  • Investor Day raised the long-term revenue target from EUR 1.5B-1.9B to EUR 1.7B-2.2B and the operating-margin target from 40%-55% to 45%-55%. These are targets, not current earnings.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• BESI remains first-tier in this advanced-packaging equipment group on business quality, purity, and operating proof; value capture is no longer dependent on one HBM narrative.
  • Continued customer expansion, repeat production orders, and orders-to-revenue conversion would support higher equipment content and installed-base demand.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• That the roughly 60% AI order mix is permanent or all new orders convert on schedule.
  • Production volume, revenue contribution, and concentration for each of the 21 hybrid-bonding customers.
  • A year-by-year revenue, margin, and cash-flow bridge to the long-term targets.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Q3 revenue growth below the +10% guidance floor or gross margin below 63%.
  • Material hybrid-bonding/AI order delays or cancellations, or stalled repeat-customer adoption.
  • Q2 operating cash flow was only EUR 47.7M, about 54% of net income, while receivables rose from EUR 186.4M to EUR 254.1M; two more quarters of poor conversion would lower earnings quality.
  • Conversion of the 2029 notes issued 1.5M treasury shares. More dilution before the earnings bridge is visible would reduce per-share value.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Context / Market-found hybrid-bonding and advanced-assembly equipment benchmark. The durable entity holds role, evidence, and kill criteria; current action is carried by BESI Q2 2026 Current-Live Deep Dive and TV Execution Zones as selected by the registry.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Ballard sells PEM fuel-cell stacks, modules, and systems across transport and stationary/backup-power use cases. In this wiki it is only a validation sample for whether hydrogen fuel cells can become repeatable commercial data-center power, not a general facility-electrical infrastructure company.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: the hydrogen-pilot branch of spine 7, Onsite Bridge Power, Storage, and Backup
  • Boundary: this page only covers fuel-cell generation and time-to-power feasibility
  • It does not own site switchgear, rack power, cooling, EPC/MEP, or any spine-8 infrastructure delivery in Facility Electrical, Rack Power, Cooling, and Delivery

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Realized results: the local filing and product/project captures prove that the company does operate a stationary fuel-cell business and has discussed data-center-relevant demonstrations or stationary-power use.
  • Forward path: the AI/data-center narrative reaches revenue only if issuer disclosure starts naming data-center customers, repeat orders, associated revenue/backlog, or verifiable installed deployments.
  • Current conclusion: the existing filing does not break stationary activity into verifiable data-center commercial results.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Filing / issuer-primary: the Q1 2026 filed materials are the current boundary for disclosed monetization.
  • Product / project evidence: the local raw packet preserves a data-center demonstration capture and a stationary-power order capture, which are enough to prove pathway relevance.
  • Conclusion: the evidence currently stops at product and pilot relevance, not repeat AI/data-center revenue proof.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Company materials present its stationary fuel-cell platform as usable for backup or continuous-power scenarios and include data-center-adjacent demonstration or order language.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: That is enough to keep BLDP as a hydrogen-pilot benchmark, but not enough to return it to the ordinary onsite-power ranking, and not enough to treat it as a spine-8 facility-infrastructure beneficiary.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Named data-center customers and repeat deployments
  • Separable data-center revenue, backlog, or gross-profit contribution
  • Hydrogen-supply, uptime, and unit economics that support repeat scale-out

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later issuer evidence still cannot move the data-center narrative into verifiable commercial results, BLDP stays context-only and does not regain higher maintenance priority
  • If future evidence shows the path remains mostly demonstrational and not repeatable in commercial deployment, it can leave ongoing spine-7 maintenance

docs.title: Durable evidence and boundary

docs.title: BX — Blackstone
docs.text: Last updated: 2026-07-13 CEST

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text:
• Structural status: context
  • Current role: Market-found
  • Primary lane: Phase 5 E10 cross-theme portfolio; alternative-asset / private-markets benchmark
  • Boundary: BX's durable role is the alternative-asset benchmark across private equity, real estate, private credit, infrastructure, and wealth channels; it is not a standalone AI revenue name and it does not absorb bank, payments, application-owner, or physical-infrastructure-owner roles
  • Action pointer: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: In the local issuer packet, BX is presented as an alternative-asset platform spanning private equity, real estate, Credit & Insurance, infrastructure, and wealth-distribution products such as BREIT and BCRED. Its E10 role is to show how private markets absorb AI-buildout spillover into real assets, private credit, insurance capital, and private-wealth distribution, not to create a tenth AI / data-center supply spine.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: For BX, AI is at most an indirect asset-allocation and capital-flow bridge. If AI buildout raises demand for data-center real estate, infrastructure, financing, private-credit deployment, or private-wealth allocation into alternatives, BX can benefit through fundraising, asset deployment, management fees, performance fees, and exit activity. But the current local issuer packet does not disclose a separate AI revenue line, and it does not turn broad platform actuals into direct AI monetization proof.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The local overview / events packet explicitly shows a platform spanning private equity, real estate, Credit & Insurance, and infrastructure.
  • The local sources also list BREIT, BCRED, private credit, and private infrastructure as visible wealth and private-capital channels.
  • The local events packet confirms formal disclosure entry points for Blackstone Fourth-Quarter & Full-Year 2025 Earnings and Blackstone First-Quarter 2026 Earnings.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company surfaces private credit, private infrastructure, credit & insurance, and private-wealth products prominently in public platform structure, indicating where management focus sits.
  • The earnings / events pages are the formal path for actuals and outlook, but the current local packet here is stronger as platform and disclosure-path proof than as AI revenue proof.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI buildout continues to pull on real estate, power-adjacent infrastructure, private financing, and sponsor-backed capital demand, BX should benefit through its existing private-markets platform.
  • That benefit depends first on fundraising, deployment, and exit efficiency rather than on any specifically named AI product line.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AI has become a separately trackable BX revenue bucket.
  • The current local packet proves an independent AI contribution to management fees, performance fees, or realizations.
  • BX should absorb the roles of banks, payment networks, server or power-equipment owners, or application owners.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later local issuer / SEC packets cannot connect platform breadth to clearer reported disclosure, this page should stay benchmark-level context.
  • If the page turns broad alternative-asset platform actuals into direct AI monetization proof, it should revert to the stricter indirect-bridge framing.
  • If the role drifts into bank ownership, physical-infrastructure ownership, or software / application ownership, the boundary is wrong.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Context / Market-found alternative-asset and private-markets benchmark. E10 keeps only the cross-theme capital-allocation role; current action lives in Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger.

docs.text:
Last updated: 2026-09-09 CEST

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for CAMT; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
• Structural status: core
  • Current role: Market-found
  • Primary lane: spine 5 advanced-packaging inspection / metrology node
  • Boundary: owns the chiplets / HBM / hybrid-bonding inspection and metrology role; does not treat CAMT as a generic semiconductor-equipment cycle name

docs.title: Business and lane position
docs.text: In the issuer raw, Camtek defines the Hawk platform directly for Chiplets, HBM and Hybrid Bonding and frames it as an advanced-packaging inspection / metrology tool spanning R&D through high-volume production. For spine 5, its ownership is yield, defect detection, and critical-dimension metrology rather than generic semiconductor-equipment beta.

docs.title: AI to revenue
docs.text: The AI transmission has already reached named orders and platform demand. The company disclosed a roughly $25 million Hawk order from a tier-1 IDM for AI applications and said total Hawk orders from that same customer reached about $45 million for delivery in 2026. At the same time, 2025 revenue reached $496.1 million, and management said backlog, pipeline, and customer discussions support another double-digit growth year in 2026. The cleaner framing is that AI advanced packaging has entered the order and delivery queue, while the local raw still does not provide a company-wide AI revenue ratio.

docs.title: 2026-08-10 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 revenue was a record USD 133.2M, with GAAP gross margin of 50.1% and non-GAAP gross margin of 51.4%.
  • Management reported more than USD 600M of year-to-date order intake, expected Q3 revenue of USD 158M-160M, and attributed expected advanced-packaging growth to the local platform evidence. Customer breadth, advanced-packaging-only margins, and conversion remain open.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Hawk is defined by the company as an advanced-packaging inspection / metrology platform for chiplets, HBM, and hybrid bonding, spanning R&D to high-volume production.
  • The company disclosed a roughly $25 million Hawk order from a tier-1 IDM for AI applications, with aggregate orders from that same customer at about $45 million for delivery in 2026.
  • 2025 revenue reached $496.1 million, up 16% year over year, and fourth-quarter revenue was $128.1 million, up 9% year over year.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management said the company is at the epicenter of the AI market and expects another double-digit growth year in 2026.
  • Backlog, pipeline, and ongoing customer discussions are forward-looking statements, not realized revenue.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: • As HBM, micro-bumps, chiplets, and hybrid bonding continue to increase packaging complexity, inspection and metrology content should rise with the value of yield control.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Company-wide AI revenue share.
  • The disclosed orders already prove broad customer diversification; the current disclosure is still concentrated in one tier-1 IDM.

docs.title: Company kill criteria
docs.text:
• Hawk demand remains trapped in a few programs or a single customer instead of broad platform adoption.
  • Backlog and pipeline fail to convert into 2026 revenue realization.
  • Issuer raw no longer supports a clear advanced-packaging inspection / metrology bottleneck role.

docs.text:
Updated: 2026-09-09 Industry page: Onsite Bridge Power, Storage, and Backup

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for CAT; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Caterpillar's core business is selling large engines, generator sets, and power solutions across many end markets. It sells industrial bridge / backup power equipment, not AI-pure asset ownership.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• It belongs to the Phase 5 E7 bridge / backup generation benchmark inside the generation / grid / time-to-power causal lane.
  • The role boundary stops at high-power equipment and power solutions. It does not extend into site electrical distribution, rack power, cooling, or EPC spine 8.
  • CAT is a large industrial OEM benchmark, not a utility-generation owner and not a proven AI pure play.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If data-center developers or power partners need larger onsite or supplemental power equipment, CAT can participate through engines, gensets, and project-based power solutions. That revenue sits inside a much broader industrial platform and should not be treated as pure AI revenue by default.

docs.title: 2026-08-04 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 sales and revenues were USD 20.5B, up 24% year over year; adjusted operating margin was 21.9% and adjusted EPS was USD 8.17.
  • Enterprise operating cash flow was USD 4.4B. The issuer cited strong order rates and backlog across its primary segments, while the local evidence does not isolate data-center economics.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The local issuer-primary capture includes a long-term Caterpillar and Hunt Energy agreement to deliver power solutions for data centers.
  • The local results and manufacturing captures are enough to establish Caterpillar's large-scale power-equipment and manufacturing capability, not a concept-only mapping.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Company materials place data-center demand inside the power-solutions / power-generation narrative.
  • Caterpillar presents itself as a platform supplier for large industrial power equipment and solutions.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• CAT works best as Phase 5 E7 context / benchmark because it shows how a large industrial OEM participates in data-center power demand.
  • It is genuinely relevant to data-center power, but it should not be written up as an AI pure play.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The page does not isolate AI-only or data-center-only revenue, backlog, or segment economics.
  • The page does not prove that data-center demand dominates Caterpillar's overall operating results.
  • The page also does not prove that Hunt-type projects will scale into a large repeatable pool of pure data-center revenue.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If future issuer-primary or filing evidence stops connecting Caterpillar power solutions to data-center use cases, this page's role should be downgraded.
  • If Hunt-type agreements fail to produce repeat deployment or revenue evidence, the data-center linkage should fall back to a weaker benchmark description.
  • If data-center power exposure becomes fully diluted by the broader industrial cycle, this page should leave the focused Phase 5 E7 browse set.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: context / benchmark; modifier: Bridge / Benchmark. This page keeps CAT as a large industrial power OEM reference point rather than as an AI-pure mainline name.

docs.text:
Role: spine 2 alternative accelerator / wafer-scale system Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Bridge / Benchmark Evidence through: 2026-08-12

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for CBRS; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Cerebras earns from wafer-scale systems, hardware, cloud capacity, and related services for fast training/inference. It is a rare non-GPU public name, but technical scarcity comes with customer concentration, project financing, data-center leases, and losses. Revenue growth is proven; durable economics are not.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: CBRS is an alternative accelerator/system architecture in Semiconductors and Foundational Compute. TSMC fabricates WSE, so wafer realization remains in Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. Selling cloud/service capacity does not make Cerebras a hyperscale demand owner.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Customers buy systems/hardware or consume cloud/service compute. OpenAI/AWS relationships may expand deployment and distribution, but value capture depends on MW going live, utilization, gross margin, customer diversification, leases/capex, and financing terms.

docs.title: 2026-08-12 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 revenue was USD 224.9M, up 87% year over year; core revenue was USD 216.0M and cloud revenue was USD 107.1M.
  • GAAP gross margin was 44.3% and GAAP net loss was USD 25.6M. The company raised full-year core-revenue outlook to USD 880M-890M, while concentration, utilization, financing, and capital intensity remain open.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 GAAP revenue was USD 193.406M, up 94%; cloud and other services revenue was USD 82.813M, up 178%.

  • GAAP gross margin was about 44.6%; GAAP operating loss was USD 15.037M.

  • Cerebras disclosed an OpenAI multi-year deal exceeding USD 20B / 750MW and an AWS partnership; Customer A/B were still 63%/11% of Q1 revenue.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • Prior FY2026 core revenue guidance was USD 855-865M, with core operating-margin guidance of (28)%-(32)%. The August 12 Q2 update raised revenue guidance to USD 880M-890M; the local Q2 capture does not update that historical operating-margin guide, and the older revenue range is superseded. The OpenAI/AWS relationships and wafer-scale inference path are presented as large-scale low-latency deployment. Contract disclosure does not prove deployment cadence, utilization, or margin.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: For some latency-sensitive inference, on-chip memory and wafer-scale architecture may offer a different TCO/latency trade-off from GPU clusters.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: The >USD20B headline is not near-term revenue or risk-free backlog. The OpenAI loan, USD 2.3B of uncommenced data-center lease payments, warrants, and concentration remain central.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Revenue/guide grows while gross margin, operating loss, or cash burn deteriorates.
  • OpenAI/AWS deployment, utilization, payment, or service-credit cadence slips materially.
  • Concentration does not fall and new customers fail to generate repeat revenue.
  • Leases, loan, warrants, or capex make per-share economics lag revenue badly.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: CBRS is an Active / Bridge / Benchmark alternative-compute entity. It has moved beyond IPO concept proof, while concentration, financing, and deployment economics still require closure.

docs.text: Role: Phase 5 E7 spine 7 generation / grid / time-to-power; CEG owns nuclear generation and contracted data-center power Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-06

docs.title: 2026-08-06 Q2 earnings update
docs.text:
• Adjusted operating-EPS guidance rose to $11.50-$12.50, while Crane received the FERC CIR-transfer waiver and NRC fuel-license approval.
  • The company also signed 920 MW of additional long-term clean/reliable generation PPAs; Calpine integration and contract economics still need validation.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Constellation is a large competitive power platform built on nuclear generation. After Calpine, it combines the largest nuclear fleet in the U.S. with complementary gas, geothermal, and storage assets plus a retail/commercial power platform.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Within Power Generation, Grid, and Fuel Supply, CEG primary-owns nuclear generation and contracted data-center power. It owns the nuclear and flexible-power fleet, commercial electricity supply, and long-duration contracted power relationships. Its ownership stops at the site / utility handoff; inside-the-fence electrical distribution, cooling, EPC, and server / network layers do not belong here.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI load first becomes long-term power demand, then shows up in CEG's nuclear output, capacity, clean attributes, and commercial contracting capability. For data centers, revenue can come from existing nuclear supply or site-level contracted power arrangements such as Freestone. The monetized product is electricity and contracted power delivery, not the data-center's internal electrical system.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The 2025 10-K disclosed that after the 2026-01-07 Calpine close, CEG had about 55 GW of generation capacity, including about 22 GW of nuclear capacity across 25 units, and served about 2.5M customer accounts.
  • The 10-K disclosed a 20-year Microsoft PPA supporting the restart of Crane Clean Energy Center.
  • Q1 2026 results also disclosed 44,666 GWh of nuclear generation in the quarter, a 92.3% owned nuclear capacity factor, and no non-refueling outage days at operated sites.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company expects Crane to provide about 835 MW of emissions-free capacity once restarted; restart still depends on regulatory approvals, interconnection-related construction, licensing, and execution timing.
  • Q1 2026 results disclosed that PUCT approved the net-metering application for the Freestone / CyrusOne data-center co-location arrangement, subject to conditions; the company also cited an existing 380 MW agreement and an additional 380 MW Phase 2 exclusive agreement.
  • Management frames the combined Calpine + nuclear platform as positioned to serve data centers, advanced manufacturing, and critical infrastructure with clean, reliable, and flexible power.
  • The Freestone data-center setup remains explicitly conditional.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• CEG's distinct ownership is not just "it has nuclear." It combines existing nuclear baseload, Calpine's flexible power fleet, and a commercial contracting platform into a long-duration contracted power offering.
  • That still does not make all nuclear, retail, or Calpine revenue AI revenue. AI monetization should appear first in specific contracts and sites.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The actual Crane restart schedule, the full Phase 2 Freestone buildout, and the eventual share of CEG earnings tied to data-center contracts are not yet proven by reported results.
  • The platform's full clean-power revenue base should not be broadly extrapolated into AI monetization.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• The Microsoft / Crane contract path or restart path fails in a material way.
  • The Freestone approval, contracting, or actual delivery path breaks down.
  • Nuclear fleet reliability, capacity factors, or effective operating life deteriorate enough to weaken long-duration power delivery.
  • Calpine integration fails to strengthen, and instead weakens, CEG's ability to serve large-load contracted power demand.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
CEG is the Core / Market-found nuclear generation and contracted data-center power platform on the generation spine. The ownership here is site-level power supply, not campus-internal electrical or server ownership.

Current action is routed only through the registry-selected VST, CEG, and TLN Current Live Research Conclusion.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Celestica is a manufacturing, design, supply-chain, and platform-solutions company organized into CCS and ATS. For spine 6, the relevant segment is CCS, especially HPS: enterprise data communications, servers and storage, routers, switches, data center interconnects, and related platform design/manufacturing.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: In spine 6, CLS is a manufacturing/integration exposure. It is not a branded systems vendor, and it should not be lazily flattened into "just another ODM/EMS." It sits closer to hyperscaler data-center hardware, switching platforms, and complex platform delivery, but its boundary remains manufacturing, engineering, and delivery rather than end-product brand control.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2026 revenue was USD 4.05B, up 53% year over year; within that, CCS revenue was USD 3.24B, up 76%, with CCS margin of 8.6%.
  • In the same quarter, HPS revenue was about USD 1.7B, up 63% year over year.
  • Q4 2025 disclosed HPS revenue of about USD 1.4B, up 72% year over year; the company also disclosed U.S. capacity expansion supporting Google TPU systems and a third hyperscaler 1.6T switching platform program.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The annual report defines CCS as the communications and enterprise (servers and storage) business and explicitly says its products can include routers, switches, data center interconnects, servers, and storage-related products.
  • Q1 FY2026 disclosed USD 3.24B of CCS revenue, USD 1.7B of HPS revenue, and the related growth and margin profile.
  • The Q4 2025 release disclosed that Celestica is Google's preferred manufacturing partner for data center hardware and systems and that it won a third hyperscaler 1.6T switching platform design-and-manufacturing program.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The prior FY2026 revenue/adjusted-EPS outlook of USD 19.0B / 10.15 is superseded by the Q2 update to USD 20.5B / 11.30 above. The stronger 2027 visibility remains forward-looking.
  • The Google TPU U.S. expansion and 2027 ramp timing are roadmap statements, not completed outcomes.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• CLS fits better as a hyperscaler AI data-center hardware manufacturing and delivery partner than as a generic EMS discount case.
  • But it monetizes AI mainly through platform manufacturing, engineering, and delivery, not through the brand or final-system pricing power of a branded systems vendor.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• How much of CCS/HPS revenue can be strictly attributed to AI rather than broader cloud or networking refresh.
  • The duration, unit economics, and margin structure of each hyperscaler program.
  • The long-run margin lift to consolidated results from Google, 1.6T switching, and co-packaged-optics programs.

docs.title: 2026-08-19 Q2 10-Q follow-up
docs.text:
• Official Q2 FY2026 evidence upgraded the platform-manufacturing proof: revenue was USD 4.70B (+62% YoY), CCS revenue USD 3.81B (+84% YoY), HPS revenue about USD 1.9B (+58% YoY, 41% of revenue), adjusted EPS $2.54, and adjusted operating margin 8.2%.
  • Management raised FY2026 outlook to revenue USD 20.5B, adjusted EPS $11.30, adjusted operating margin 8.4%, and free cash flow USD 600M; it also said 2027 revenue growth should accelerate beyond the expected 2026 65% growth rate.
  • The 10-Q confirms material concentration: three CCS customers represented 32% / 17% / 14% of Q2 revenue (63% combined). H1 non-GAAP FCF was USD 285.0M, while H1 capex reached USD 493.3M.
  • Official Q2 deck/replay route: CLOSED; Q&A substance: PARTIAL. HPS program duration and customer-program economics are BLOCKED-PUBLIC-DISCLOSURE; 1.6T / AI Compute pathway language is not evidence of a contract term, minimum commitment, or return.
  • The 8/5-8/6 equity offering issued 11,129,031 shares, approximately 9.68% of the old 114,982,086 shares outstanding on 7/22. The Q2 USD 11.30 adjusted-EPS outlook assumed no share issuance in the remainder of 2026; no revised per-share bridge followed the offering, so the pre-offering calculation cannot be used directly for diluted-share analysis.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• CCS/HPS growth slows materially without replacement platform wins.
  • Hyperscaler platform programs are delayed, cancelled, or reduced to low-value pass-through manufacturing.
  • Customer concentration worsens further and makes revenue or cash flow too dependent on a few programs.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
Active / Market-found manufacturing/integration exposure in spine 6. CLS matters because it already has explicit hyperscaler platform-manufacturing proof, but it still should not be conflated with DELL or with every other ODM.
