It does not absorb SOFI's digital-bank and lending platform, AFRM's BNPL merchant network, or a generic application or infrastructure-owner role.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Cortex Digests and Cortex Assistant currently sit in the in-app insight, education, and service-experience layer. If they improve engagement, retention, Gold adoption, or transaction and asset usage, value still appears through existing subscription and financial-entry economics. AI is not separately disclosed as revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Official IR materials, the about page, and the Q1 FY2026 8-K frame Robinhood as a broader financial-services entry point for a new generation of investors.
  • The Q1 FY2026 packet records 4.3 million Robinhood Gold subscribers and USD 50 million in Gold subscription revenue. Those are subscription actuals, not AI-attributed revenue.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company says Cortex Digests has been used by nearly 1 million customers and describes Cortex Assistant as an AI-powered insights tool still rolling out.
  • Those statements prove product deployment and usage, not standalone AI monetization.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If Cortex improves research, education, and service experience, it may increase engagement, retention, and Gold value.
  • The result must be verified in paid, asset-retention, or usage outcomes rather than inferred from rollout alone.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Cortex has created separable revenue or profit contribution.
  • Broad transaction, crypto, subscription, or asset growth is directly attributable to AI.
  • HOOD should absorb SOFI, AFRM, or a wider application or infrastructure role.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Lower trading and crypto activity would directly weaken transaction-driven economics.
  • If Gold growth does not produce steadier retention and unit economics, subscription support weakens.
  • If Cortex continues to show only usage or rollout claims without paid or retention outcomes, AI remains an experience layer.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: HPS.A is an Active / Market-found transformer / power-quality company with the body-only modifier former-half-hidden. It sits in the medium- and low-voltage distribution layer between the site electrical boundary and the energized rack. It benefits from data-center expansion and custom electrical demand, but it does not own E7 generation, E2 compute silicon, or E6 full systems.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
HPS.A's core products are dry-type transformers, power-quality products, and custom-engineered electrical solutions. The position is after power enters the site or building and before power reaches rack-level electrical equipment.

Its boundaries need to stay explicit: - It does not own E7 generation / grid / time-to-power assets and should not be reframed as a generation or utility-power name. - It does not own E2 compute silicon, so GPU or ASIC demand cannot be treated as HPS.A revenue by default. - It does not own E6 systems integration, so full rack, server, or site delivery should not be assigned to HPS.A.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
AI data-center expansion increases demand for internal distribution, voltage transformation, harmonic mitigation, and custom electrical content. HPS.A monetizes that through dry-type transformers, power-quality equipment, and custom-engineered distribution content rather than through AI software or server branding.

That mechanism still has to stay under issuer-claim discipline: the company has explicitly linked data-center expansion to custom-product demand, but it has not disclosed named hyperscalers, an AI revenue split, or a data-center backlog percentage.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• In its annual report, HPS.A defines itself as a supplier of dry-type transformers and power-quality solutions serving North American electrical and industrial end markets.
  • FY2025 results materials show record sales, backlog growth, and expansion in private-label / custom-engineered solutions.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The official Data Centers page targets data centers as an explicit vertical with relevant product and solution positioning; that is company positioning, not customer-purchase or revenue proof.
  • Management links part of the growth to datacentre expansion and demand for custom-engineered solutions.
  • Company framing supports the idea that HPS.A supplies customized transformer and distribution-related content for data-center deployments.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI campuses keep expanding, medium- and low-voltage distribution plus power-quality demand inside the site should rise with them, creating more opportunity for HPS.A's custom electrical content.
  • HPS.A monetizes longer-cycle project electrical content rather than the faster and more direct power ramps seen in GPU or rack-PSU names.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• It is not yet proven that HPS.A has attributable revenue from a named hyperscaler or AI campus deployment.
  • It is not yet proven how much of backlog can be cleanly split into data-center or AI-related orders.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later issuer-primary materials stop linking data-center expansion to custom-engineered growth, this page should be downgraded.
  • If revenue becomes mainly a broad industrial or commercial cycle story again and data centers fall back to a minor footnote, the core framing should shrink.
  • If new evidence shows HPS.A's role in data centers is mostly generic replacement content rather than specification-driven electrical infrastructure, the page needs to be rewritten.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
Active / Market-found; modifier: former-half-hidden. The E8 role is transformer / power quality from the site electrical boundary to the energized rack, with a hard boundary at not owning E7 generation, E2 compute silicon, or E6 systems.

docs.text:
Updated: 2026-09-09 CEST Industry page: Financial Institutions and Capital Markets Classification: Direct

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for HSBC; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: Chain position
docs.text: Cross-border corporate banking, wealth management, and international network banking in Asia.

docs.title: Why it is on this chain
docs.text: The 2026 interim results move HSBC's cross-border network, Asian wealth franchise, and transaction bank from a static moat description into current operating proof: Wealth fee and other income rose 18% in 1H26, Asia net new money reached USD 57B, and Wholesale Transaction Banking fee and other income grew 4% on a constant-currency basis.

docs.title: Operating evidence
docs.text: Cross-border flows across Asia and the Middle East, trade banking, and wealth management remain the hardest-to-replicate moat. Reported 1H26 revenue was USD 37.742B / +11% and PBT USD 19.522B / +23%; the cleaner constant-currency ex-notable comparison also grew, to revenue of USD 38.168B and PBT of USD 20.395B, so the improvement is not only a low-base effect from the 1H25 BoCom notable items.

docs.title: Key risks
docs.text:
• 1H26 ECL of USD 2.353B / 47bps was above 42bps a year earlier; Hong Kong CRE, Middle East uncertainty, and pockets of mid-market credit stress remain open.
  • CET1 of 14.1% was below 14.9% at 2025 year-end as the Hang Seng Bank privatisation, dividends, RWA growth, and the resumed buy-back all use capital capacity.
  • Fifteen announced business or market exits, the USD 2B simplification-savings target, and reinvestment raise execution complexity. China/Hong Kong/UK macro, geopolitics, and cross-border rules can still alter the path.

docs.title: 2026-08-04 1H26 earnings update
docs.text:
• Annualised RoTE was 18.2%, or 19.1% excluding notable items; 2026 banking-NII guidance moved from around USD 46B to at least USD 46B.
  • The second interim dividend was USD 0.10/share, and HSBC announced an up to USD 1B buy-back. Capital return has resumed, but CET1 and credit risks remain.

docs.title: One-line view
docs.text: 【International bank】1H26 strengthened the Asian wealth, transaction-banking, and cross-border-network proof, while capital, credit, geopolitical, and restructuring risks remain operating constraints.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Hubbell is the E8 electrical equipment and connectivity platform from the grid toward the site boundary, turning grid-to-site connection, protection, and electrical attachment into a usable site-entry condition.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: HUBB's primary lane is electrical and utility equipment plus connectivity context: transmission and distribution components, substation-related hardware, connectors, protection, grounding, communications, and site-entry electrical accessories. It is an equipment owner, not an EPC contractor; it does not own rack-side UPS or thermal infrastructure, and it does not own upstream generation and fuel assets or server and networking-system manufacturing.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: An AI campus first needs power that can be connected, protected, and handed into the site before in-building distribution and rack energization matter. Load-center expansion raises the amount and specification of utility, substation, site-entry, and datacenter electrical products, and Hubbell monetizes that grid-to-site electrical content.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The FY2025 10-K and the Q1 2026 10-Q and earnings call show HUBB spanning Utility Solutions and Electrical Solutions across utility-side and site-side electrical hardware.
  • In Q1 2026 management explicitly discussed growth tied to data center and Grid Infrastructure demand, with hyperscaler, colocation, transmission, and substation demand inside the current business context.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management frames datacenter demand, grid modernization, load growth, and the 765kV transmission opportunity as important future demand sources.
  • The May 2026 NSI 8-K, press release, and term-loan 8-K establish that Hubbell signed and arranged financing for the transaction; if it closes, NSI's electrical fittings, connectors, wire-management, and related datacenter and network-infrastructure products would extend Electrical Solutions.
  • The NSI deal framing stresses complementarity with Electrical Solutions and names datacenter and network infrastructure as strategic verticals; that is issuer growth framing, not a disclosed AI revenue breakout.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If hyperscaler and colocation campuses expand and require more site-entry electrical work, a platform like Hubbell should benefit from higher electrical content per site even without owning downstream rack power.
  • HUBB's durable E8 anchor value is that it keeps ownership of the "can power safely enter the site and connect reliably into the facility" layer, rather than collapsing that ownership into EPC execution or rack thermal systems.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local evidence does not isolate AI revenue for HUBB, and it does not prove that datacenter-related electrical growth will durably outgrow the broader utility and electrical base business.
  • The current local evidence does not support HUBB owning utility interconnection EPC, substation construction execution, or rack and facility thermal infrastructure; those remain separate owners.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later disclosure shows datacenter electrical demand was only a short-lived order spike without sustained content or attach, the E8 anchor thesis weakens.
  • If NSI integration reduces execution quality or fails to deepen datacenter and site-entry content, the current boundary call should be revisited.
  • If the page starts treating HUBB as an EPC contractor, a time-to-power asset owner, or a rack-thermal owner without local-source support, that is a kill signal.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Role: Core / Market-found. Stable E8 owner for grid-to-site electrical equipment and connectivity context; not an E7 generation/fuel owner and not an E6 server or networking-system manufacturer.

docs.text: Role: spine 2 x86 CPU/host-compute context; foundry is a secondary spine 5 role Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Bridge / Benchmark Evidence through: 2026-04-23; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Intel earns from client/server CPUs and platform products while operating a capital-intensive foundry. Its direct compute mechanism is host CPU and DCAI demand. Foundry/advanced packaging is a separate manufacturing thesis with different economics and cannot be used to blur product and factory execution.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: INTC's primary context is the x86 CPU/host node in Semiconductors and Foundational Compute. Intel Foundry and advanced packaging secondary-link Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials; manufacturing revenue, internal transfers, and external-customer proof require separate analysis.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI servers and agentic inference can increase host CPU, I/O, and platform demand, becoming DCAI product revenue. Foundry must earn wafer/package revenue through yield, volume, customer commitments, utilization, and capex returns; CPU growth is not foundry proof.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 revenue was USD 13.6B, up 7%; DCAI revenue was USD 5.1B, up 22%.
  • GAAP gross margin was 39.4% and GAAP operating margin (23.1)%; non-GAAP operating margin was 12.3%.
  • Quarterly cash from operations was USD 1.1B, leaving material profitability/cash constraints.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Management says inference/agentic AI raises CPU, wafer, and advanced-packaging demand and stresses factory-network supply. External foundry customers, volume, and returns remain incomplete.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: AI systems still require host CPUs, so Intel can benefit from CPU refresh and platform attach even if accelerators capture most value.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: DCAI growth does not prove foundry success. Product improvement does not prove external foundry share, yield, or ROIC, and manufacturing capex is not AI revenue.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• DCAI share/revenue slows and server CPU competitiveness fades.
  • Foundry yield, external customers, or utilization do not improve while capex consumes cash.
  • GAAP/non-GAAP gaps, restructuring, or asset burdens expand persistently.
  • Product and manufacturing roadmaps are delayed together.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: INTC is Context / Bridge / Benchmark: CPU is compute context and foundry is a secondary spine 5 thesis.

docs.title: JCI — Johnson Controls
docs.text: Role: Phase 5 E8 spine 8 site electrical boundary to energized rack; JCI is the cooling / building-controls benchmark with an explicit proof gate Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Bridge / Benchmark Evidence through: 2026-04-21; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Johnson Controls is a building cooling, controls, and data-center-solutions platform, not a pure AI cooling winner. In E8 it serves as the cooling / building-controls benchmark, but any hidden framing must clear a stricter source gate first.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: JCI sits after the site electrical boundary and around the operating room layer: Applied HVAC, Silent-Aire, YORK, thermal management, building automation and controls, security, and fire protection. It does not own upstream generation / fuel, and it does not own E6 servers / network systems. It sells the thermal / controls stack at the building and data-hall layer.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As AI data-center power density and uptime requirements rise, cooling, high-density thermal management, controls, monitoring, fire protection, and security all scale with it. JCI monetizes that through data-center solutions, Applied HVAC, modular data-center cooling, building controls, and related services, not through servers or network equipment themselves.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The official release, 10-Q, and earnings slides jointly support the conclusion that Americas orders and backlog growth were primarily driven by data-center projects.
  • The 10-Q explicitly says Americas organic growth was led by Applied HVAC and Controls.
  • The 10-Q describes Johnson Controls as a platform around energy efficiency, decarbonization, thermal management, and mission-critical performance, explicitly naming data centers as one of the rapidly expanding industries it serves.
  • The data-center and thermal-management product pages show a real current solutions stack across YORK, Silent-Aire, thermal management, building controls, security, and fire protection.
  • The data-center page describes Silent-Aire as a data-center-solutions leader focused on Modular Data Centers, CRAC, and CRAHU systems.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company positions itself as a dedicated global data-center solutions partner and emphasizes hundreds of successful data-center projects, global scalability, and engineered consistency.
  • Management raised FY26 guidance in the Q1 results materials, but that guidance should not be treated as a direct AI-cooling attribution.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• JCI is a broad cooling / building-controls benchmark rather than a pure-play AI cooling name because monetization is spread across HVAC, thermal management, controls, safety, and services.
  • Data-center project momentum is real, but it is better read as a repricing entry point for a building-systems platform than as a fully closed hidden-name thesis.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current raw packet does not provide clean data-center revenue share, standalone high-density-cooling revenue or margin, or clearer named-customer / attach-rate proof.
  • needs-source-before-any-hidden-gate must remain in force: without cleaner source-backed revenue mix or project monetization proof, JCI should not be upgraded into a hidden-thesis conclusion.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later materials stop supporting the claim that Americas orders / backlog are primarily data-center-driven, JCI's data-center read-through should be downgraded.
  • If the cooling / controls / safety stack remains broad but still lacks measurable revenue or margin proof, the benchmark role should not be upgraded.
  • If broader building exposure dilutes the data-center increment, or competition compresses thermal-management project margins, JCI should remain bridge / benchmark only.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: JCI's current role is Context/benchmark; its formal state is Bridge / Benchmark. needs-source-before-any-hidden-gate remains only a workflow modifier, meaning any hidden framing requires harder source-backed monetization proof first.

docs.title: JPM — JPMorgan Chase
docs.text: Last updated: 2026-07-13 CEST

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text:
• Structural status: context
  • Current role: Market-found
  • Primary lane: Phase 5 E10 cross-theme portfolio; universal-bank benchmark
  • Boundary: JPM's durable role is the large universal-bank base that shows how deposits, lending, payments, custody, investment banking, and wealth distribution absorb corporate and market activity; it is not a standalone AI revenue name and it does not absorb payment-network, fintech, consumer-credit, application-owner, or physical-infrastructure-owner roles
  • Action pointer: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: In the local issuer packet, JPM appears as a large universal-bank platform spanning Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management, with dedicated technology and quarterly-disclosure entry points. Its E10 value is as a benchmark for how macro conditions and AI-capex spillover reach the large-bank base, not as part of any AI / data-center supply spine.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: For JPM, AI is at most an indirect bridge, not a standalone revenue bucket. If AI capex and enterprise expansion create more financing, trading, payments, treasury, custody, and wealth-allocation activity, JPM can earn more through its existing universal-bank and investment-banking engines via fees, net interest income, and asset-management-related revenue; technology may also improve internal efficiency. But the current local issuer sources do not disclose AI as a separate revenue line, so broad bank-level actuals cannot be written up as AI monetization proof.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The local IR packet explicitly lists Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management as core platforms.
  • The company maintains a separate quarterly-earnings hub; the current packet does not break AI out as a reporting line.
  • The current local sources do not disclose a standalone AI revenue bucket.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Technology is an explicit capability area in official IR navigation, showing that the company treats technology and operations as part of its operating infrastructure.
  • The quarterly-earnings page is the formal management channel for actual results and forward-looking commentary, but the current local packet does not break AI out as a reporting segment.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI increases corporate treasury, capital raising, market making, payments, custody, and wealth-allocation activity, JPM should benefit through its existing universal-bank machine.
  • That benefit is better understood as spillover from client activity and internal efficiency than as a new AI product revenue bucket.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AI has become a separately trackable revenue or profit disclosure.
  • AI-related client activity is already large enough to dominate the bank's earnings profile.
  • JPM should absorb the roles of V — Visa, SOFI — SoFi Technologies, AFRM — Affirm Holdings, or any infrastructure owner.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later local issuer / SEC packets show that this page is missing more specific bank-segment or quarter-actual disclosure, raw evidence should be refreshed before the judgment is strengthened.
  • If the page drifts back into treating broad bank earnings as AI revenue proof, it should revert to the stricter indirect-bridge framing.
  • If the role drifts into payment-network, fintech, consumer-credit, or data-center asset ownership, the boundary is wrong.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Context / Market-found universal-bank benchmark. E10 keeps only the cross-theme financial-base role; current action lives in Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger.

docs.title: KLAR — Klarna Group
docs.text: Role: E10 cross-theme portfolio prose; BNPL, digital-bank, and merchant-consumer network owner Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence as of: 2026-08-18

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Klarna's stable position is a merchant-consumer network that ties together BNPL, merchant payments, consumer entry points, and digital-bank relationships. This is first a consumer-finance network and user-relationship owner, not B2B credit-decisioning infrastructure and not an ecommerce platform or broader application / infrastructure owner.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: KLAR sits on the fintech / consumer-credit side of E10 cross-theme portfolio prose. Its stable ownership is BNPL, digital-bank, and merchant-consumer network. It does not absorb UPST's AI/ML lending marketplace, PGY's B2B credit-decisioning / securitization infrastructure, or PDD's commerce / application-owner role.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Klarna's AI relevance shows up more in risk control, personalization, service automation, and merchant / consumer matching efficiency, but those all serve BNPL and network economics. Revenue first comes from payments, merchant relationships, and consumer-finance relationships, not a separable AI revenue line. Funding, credit, merchant, or GMV metrics do not automatically equal AI proof.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Local issuer source positions Klarna as a global digital bank and flexible-payments provider.
  • The FY2025 and Q1 FY2026 results pages provide issuer-primary operating actuals supporting the view that this is a BNPL / merchant-consumer network rather than a single-product tool.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Issuer framing consistently emphasizes flexible payments, merchant reach, consumer relationships, and digital-bank positioning.
  • That framing proves network and product positioning, but it does not by itself prove AI as a separate revenue line.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If user retention, merchant adoption, and credit control stay balanced, Klarna's network economics can continue improving.
  • That improvement belongs to BNPL and digital-bank network execution, not to B2B underwriting infrastructure or ecommerce-platform ownership.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local source set does not isolate AI revenue.
  • Funding, credit loss, merchant growth, or GMV totals are not automatic proof of AI monetization.

docs.title: 2026-08-18 Q2 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q2 GMV was USD 36.6B, revenue USD 1.042B, transaction margin dollars USD 446M, adjusted operating income USD 91M, operating income USD 27M, and net income USD 9M.
  • FY2026 GMV guidance moved from above USD 155B to USD 149B-151B, and revenue guidance from above USD 4.34B to USD 4.08B-4.16B. Q3 revenue guidance of USD 940M-980M is below Q2 actual.
  • Unit-economics and profitability evidence improved while the growth/volume outlook reset. No call replay, transcript, or Q&A was captured.

docs.title: Value capture and boundary of misread
docs.text: Klarna captures value by combining consumer entry points, payment scenarios, merchant distribution, and bank-like account relationships into a high-frequency network. The misread boundary is turning it into B2B credit infrastructure, a pure lending marketplace, or rewriting merchant / consumer growth directly as AI monetization. KLAR owns the BNPL / digital-bank / merchant-consumer network role here.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If credit losses, funding costs, or regulation damage network economics, margin room contracts first.
  • If merchant adoption and consumer activity fall out of balance, the network effect weakens.
  • If later local issuer / SEC evidence still consists only of broad consumer-finance totals without more specific automation or attach proof, this page should stay restrained on AI-relevance language.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
KLAR is Active / Market-found. Its stable ownership is BNPL, digital-bank, and merchant-consumer network. It does not absorb the owner boundaries of UPST, PGY, or PDD.

Current action is routed only by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; KLAR is currently none, with no fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Centrus is an upstream uranium-enrichment and nuclear-fuel supplier, especially around HALEU capability. In this wiki it represents advanced-nuclear fuel supply, not data-center onsite power, facility electrical work, or cooling delivery.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: the nuclear-fuel upstream branch of spine 7, Power Generation, Grid, and Fuel Supply
  • Boundary: this page only covers whether fuel supply can support faster time-to-power for advanced nuclear
  • It does not own site switchgear, rack power, cooling, EPC/MEP, or any spine-8 infrastructure delivery in Facility Electrical, Rack Power, Cooling, and Delivery

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Realized results: the local raw packet proves that the company has public HALEU milestone disclosures, a DOE contract framework, and continuing issuer reporting.
  • Forward path: AI/data-center demand matters only if advanced-reactor projects and fuel arrangements convert into verifiable deliveries and revenue.
  • Current conclusion: the local evidence proves strategic position, not realized AI-linked revenue closure.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Issuer / press release: HALEU production milestone material
  • Issuer / contract release: DOE contract and cascade-construction material
  • Issuer / annual reports: continuing corporate disclosure baseline
  • Conclusion: this is a Needs-source fuel benchmark; the local packet does not yet tie advanced-nuclear demand directly to realized revenue

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Company materials emphasize HALEU capability, government cooperation, and its strategic position in the Western nuclear-fuel chain.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: That is enough to keep LEU as spine-7 nuclear-fuel context / benchmark, but not enough to write it as a realized data-center power beneficiary.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Whether data-center-linked advanced-nuclear projects already convert into realized LEU commercial revenue
  • Whether named customers, off-take structures, or repeat fuel purchases already form a verifiable loop
  • How short the lag really is between AI-load growth and LEU financial realization

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later local evidence still cannot move the HALEU strategic story into verifiable commercial realization, LEU remains Needs-source context
  • If stronger local issuer/filing evidence shows the data-center time-to-power link remains mostly long-dated narrative, it can leave high-priority maintenance

docs.title: LITE — Lumentum
docs.text: Role: spine 4 photonic components / laser source / optical subsystem platform Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-11

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Lumentum sells the lasers, modules, and photonic subsystems behind AI optical networking. Its value is not only one module cycle; it sits across components, systems, CPO light sources, and scale-across monitoring inside the optical layer.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: LITE primary-owns the photonic-components / optical-subsystems node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI, with core exposure to EMLs, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies, pluggable modules, and higher-power light sources. It does not primary-own switch silicon or AI system assembly; scale-across monitoring and WSS exposure still belong to the optical layer rather than the compute platform itself.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As AI data centers demand more 800G, 1.6T, future 3.2T, CPO, and more complex DCI / scale-across optical links, Lumentum can raise shipments and mix through components, modules, laser sources, and some monitoring/control products. Profit depends on cloud demand, product mix, manufacturing execution, and the speed of next-platform adoption.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The investor overview describes Lumentum as a provider of optical and photonic technologies for AI, cloud computing, and next-generation communications, with products that include lasers, modules, and optical subsystems.
  • FY2025 Q4 net revenue was USD 480.7M, and Cloud & Networking revenue was USD 424.1M, or 88.2% of total revenue; management specifically highlighted strong demand in EML chips, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies for data-center interconnect, and 800G modules.
  • Q3 FY2026 net revenue was USD 808.4M, up 90.1% YoY and 21.5% QoQ; non-GAAP gross margin was 47.9%, and non-GAAP operating margin was 32.2%.
  • In Q3 FY2026 product-type revenue, Components were USD 533.3M and Systems were USD 275.1M.
  • Named OFC 2026 products included a 1.6T DR4 OSFP prototype with four 400G differential EMLs, an 800 mW SHP laser for CPO / silicon-photonics architectures, a 16-channel DWDM UHP laser source, and scale-across C-OCM / iTLA / WSS / DGE products.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• In the FY2025 Q4 results, management said AI data-center and long-haul demand gives the company confidence to surpass USD 600M in quarterly revenue by 2026-06 or earlier.
  • Prior Q4 FY2026 guidance was revenue USD 960M-1.01B, non-GAAP operating margin 35.0%-36.0%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS USD 2.85-3.05; the Q4 actual results above supersede that dated forecast.
  • Management said CPO and OCS should further increase earnings power; on this page those remain issuer claims rather than realized results.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Because Lumentum spans both components and systems, AI optical traffic growth does not need to monetize through only one module generation; multiple device and monitoring layers can convert the same networking upgrade into revenue.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Current local sources do not prove that Q3 FY2026 growth and margin levels can be linearly extrapolated for the long term.
  • Current sources do not precisely separate how much revenue and profit came from AI versus broader cloud, telecom, or other end markets.
  • When CPO, OCS, and broader scale-across products become material financial pillars is still mainly management direction rather than current proof.

docs.title: 2026-08-11 Q4 FY2026 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q4 revenue was USD 1.0063B, with non-GAAP gross margin of 50.4%, non-GAAP operating margin of 36.6%, and non-GAAP EPS of USD 3.23.
  • Components revenue was USD 649.4M and Systems revenue USD 356.9M. The Q1 FY2027 revenue guide was USD 1.225B-1.275B, with non-GAAP operating margin of 39.5%-40.5% and EPS of USD 4.05-4.35.
  • The official release and deck support the reported quarter, product mix, and company-stated AI/cloud optical drivers. They do not disclose AI-specific revenue/profit, named-customer economics, concentration, duration, or CPO/OCS/ELS/NPO revenue dollars; no Q&A transcript was captured.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Cloud AI demand slows and hits the components / modules mix first, pulling down revenue and margins.
  • Next-generation laser-source, CPO, or scale-across products fail to convert into volume production.
  • The company keeps AI-relevant products but cannot sustain component leadership and systems-level mix expansion.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
LITE is a Core / Market-found optical / photonics platform name. Q4 FY2026 advances reported financial proof across Cloud & Networking and the Components / Systems businesses, but the current sources do not separately identify AI-specific revenue or profit; further lift from CPO / OCS still needs later financial confirmation.

Current action is routed only by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; LITE is currently none, with no fallback.

docs.title: LLY — Eli Lilly
docs.text: Updated: 2026-09-09 CEST Industry page: Pharma and Biotechnology Classification: direct

docs.title: Theme position
docs.text: Large-cap pharma, metabolism leader, and GLP-1 weight-loss platform.

docs.title: Why it is in this theme
docs.text: Lilly’s most important current asset is not any single drug, but the obesity/diabetes platform unlocked around tirzepatide, along with manufacturing, commercialization, and pipeline expansion it drives.

docs.title: My current preferred bullish case
docs.text: Mounjaro / Zepbound are still scaling rapidly and capacity expansion is catching up; if non-incretin businesses keep growing, Lilly’s earnings structure will be sturdier than many expect.

docs.title: My current key risks
docs.text: The biggest risk is not demand but the combination of supply, pricing, and high expectations; if politics or payer policy start systematic pricing pressure, valuation becomes very sensitive.

docs.title: 2026-08-05 Q2 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q2 revenue increased 48% to USD 23.0B, and Key Products revenue was USD 15.7B.
  • Full-year revenue guidance rose to USD 85.0B-87.0B. Reported and non-GAAP EPS included USD 3.03 per share of acquired-Ipr&D charges.

docs.title: One-line view
docs.text:
【Pharma】The GLP-1 / GIP platform is still scaling; the biggest threat is supply, pricing, and over-expectation converging.

docs.text: Role: spine 1 owned-capacity demand benchmark; advertising/assistant provide demand feedback Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-04-29; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Meta earns mainly from Family of Apps advertising and reinvests that cash in recommendation systems, models, assistants, glasses, and owned data centers. AI already affects ad delivery and engagement, but Meta is not a merchant cloud: most infrastructure is monetized indirectly through its own products.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Meta is an owned-hyperscale capacity buyer in Cloud and Compute Demand. It creates real demand for GPU, network, power, facility, and storage supply, but recovers the investment mainly through ad prices, impressions, and retention—unlike cloud-usage revenue at MSFT/AMZN/GOOG.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Recommendation and ad models can improve engagement, impressions, conversion, and price per ad. Assistants, models, and glasses may create new entry points, but their business models remain less proven. Capex creates value only if incremental ad/product cash exceeds depreciation and operating cost.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2026 revenue was USD 56.31B, up 33%; operating margin was 41%.
  • Family daily active people were 3.56B; ad impressions rose 19% and average price per ad rose 12%.
  • Quarterly capex including finance-lease principal was USD 19.84B; FCF was USD 12.39B.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • FY2026 capex outlook increased to USD 125-145B, partly for data-center costs supporting future capacity; this is forward guidance rather than realized capex.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Advertising cash flow and first-party distribution can support long-duration model/assistant scale and improve ad effectiveness and retention.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Meta does not fully disclose standalone AI revenue or ROI. Not all ad growth is AI, and assistants, glasses, or superintelligence are not yet established high-profit revenue streams.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: Meta is a major capacity buyer and demand read-through, not an infrastructure seller. Value capture remains mostly ad economics; demand scale without engagement, pricing, or new revenue does not ensure shareholder return.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Capex/depreciation outgrow advertising revenue, operating income, and FCF.
  • AI recommendation increases usage while ad pricing, conversion, or user quality weakens.
  • Reality Labs, assistants, or glasses fail to produce durable returns.
  • Privacy, safety, youth-protection, or antitrust rules constrain data and advertising.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: META is a Context / Market-found owned-capacity demand benchmark. It validates hyperscale capex but owns no supply-chain primary node.

docs.title: Theme position
docs.text: Big-ticket oncology, vaccines, animal health, and a deep late-stage pipeline.

docs.title: Why it is in this theme

docs.title: My current preferred bullish case

docs.title: My current key risks

docs.title: MRVL — Marvell Technology
docs.text: Updated: 2026-07-13 Industry page: AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI Action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Marvell's core business is supplying switching, interconnect, optical-connectivity, and custom accelerated-infrastructure silicon for data centers and network infrastructure. It is not a general compute-platform owner.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Its primary ownership is data-center networking / optical.
  • Its secondary ownership is custom silicon / XPU exposure.
  • This page treats switching, interconnect, and optical connectivity as the first-line lens.
  • This page does not treat Marvell as a GPU, CPU, or full-system owner.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI-cluster expansion first lifts demand for switching, interconnect, optical connectivity, and custom infrastructure silicon, then flows into Marvell's data-center revenue. Custom silicon is an incremental source, not the primary ownership on this page.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• FY2026 revenue was USD 8.195B, up 42% year over year, and the results release attributed the growth to AI demand.
  • The company's data-center solutions page explicitly places Marvell in custom accelerated infrastructure silicon and data-center connectivity.
  • NVIDIA and Marvell announced an NVLink Fusion strategic partnership.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Partnership materials say the companies will collaborate on silicon photonics; that is future collaboration framing, not realized shipment or revenue.
  • Management said year-over-year growth should accelerate in each quarter of FY2027 and that bookings continue to grow.
  • NVLink Fusion materials say Marvell will provide custom XPUs and NVLink Fusion-compatible scale-up networking.
  • Partnership materials say NVIDIA invested USD 2B in Marvell, but that ecosystem language is not the same as disclosed long-term revenue share.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• MRVL's primary ownership in the AI chain belongs under networking / optical, not under a custom-silicon-only narrative.
  • Custom silicon clearly adds upside, but it remains secondary exposure and should not displace the core switching, interconnect, and optical role.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The page does not have issuer-primary line-item proof for how much revenue NVLink Fusion will generate for MRVL.
  • The page does not have enough raw evidence to allocate MRVL's share inside hyperscaler programs or the broader NVIDIA ecosystem.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later issuer-primary material no longer supports data-center networking / optical as the primary role, this page's role should be rewritten.
  • If the AI-growth story narrows to a single custom-program narrative without broader interconnect evidence, MRVL's durable role should be downgraded.
  • If partnership language persists without additional product or revenue realization, the page should not raise the weight of secondary custom-silicon exposure.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: active / Market-found. Primary ownership is networking / optical, with custom silicon kept as secondary exposure only.

docs.title: MSFT — Microsoft
docs.text: Role: spine 1 demand / capacity economics; enterprise AI production is secondary Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-04-29; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Microsoft earns Azure consumption, Microsoft 365/Dynamics/security subscriptions, and enterprise software fees. AI raises its data-center demand while creating billable Copilot, Azure AI, and agent usage. The key test is whether that usage grows fast enough to cover infrastructure investment.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: In Cloud and Compute Demand, Microsoft is a hyperscale capacity buyer and merchant-cloud operator. It also owns enterprise workflow distribution in AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle. Unlike accelerator vendors or pure application benchmarks, Microsoft controls cloud infrastructure, developer tooling, and enterprise seats.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Training, inference, and agents on Azure generate consumption revenue. Copilot, security, data, and business applications can add seats, usage, or premium bundles. Contracts enter RPO and convert as services are delivered. Economics depend on utilization, model/chip cost, capacity timing, and software attach—not capex alone.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q3 FY2026 revenue was USD 82.9B, up 18%; operating income was USD 38.4B, up 20%.
  • Microsoft Cloud revenue was USD 54.5B, up 29%; Azure and other cloud services grew 40%.
  • Commercial RPO reached USD 627B, up 99%.
  • The AI business surpassed a USD 37B annual revenue run rate, up 123%.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: The enterprise installed base and Azure distribution lower adoption friction and support cross-sell across cloud, security, data, and workflow products.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: RPO and Azure growth are not wholly AI. The disclosed AI run rate does not provide standalone margin, and durable Copilot/agent ARPU still needs usage and renewal proof.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: Microsoft's advantage is dual infrastructure and workflow distribution, not permanent leadership by one model. It is already market-found; the issue is whether AI revenue, utilization, and operating leverage outpace capex and model cost.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Azure/AI growth slows while data-center depreciation and capex keep rising.
  • Copilot or agent usage fails to become renewal, ARPU, or measurable productivity value.
  • Model partnerships/dependencies worsen cost, governance, or differentiation.
  • Security incidents, antitrust action, or bundling limits weaken distribution.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: MSFT is a Core / Market-found demand entity with a secondary AI-production link.

docs.title: MTSI — MACOM
docs.text: Role: spine 4 analog / driver copper-optical enabling components Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-06

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: MACOM is more of a lower-level component supplier inside AI networking than a headline platform winner. It sells the drivers, equalizers, and related semiconductor parts that help 1.6T / 3.2T optical transceivers and high-density copper interconnects work.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: MTSI primary-owns the enabling-components node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI, especially optical modulator drivers and scale-up copper cable driver / equalizer products. It does not primary-own full pluggable modules, switch silicon, or AI systems; the most durable role here is a component supplier inside the interconnect layer.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If AI networking keeps moving toward 400G per lane, 1.6T / 3.2T optical modules, and denser scale-up copper, MACOM can add shipments and content through drivers, equalizers, and related analog connectivity parts. Its upside comes more through component-level design wins than through owning the full platform share.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• MACOM describes itself as a semiconductor-products supplier and, on 2026-03-17, announced two new 448G PAM4 modulator drivers for next-generation 1.6T and 3.2T optical transceivers.
  • Those drivers are explicitly described as supporting 400G per lane transmission and working with silicon-photonics, EML, and TFLN modulators.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• A 2026-03-16 release positions a cable driver with equalizer for next-generation scale-up connectivity and low-power, high-density copper, and as an alternative to retimed architectures; these are product-positioning and performance claims.
  • The company says the 448G drivers can accelerate customer time-to-market for next-generation connectivity systems and support AI, ML, and HPC data-center architectures.
  • Management says the new copper cable-driver solution can increase data throughput while preserving copper’s cost and power advantages.
  • The linked MACOM PDF is only a local stub, so any broader corporate financial or product framing that may exist there is not treated as verified fact on this page.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: As long as AI interconnect upgrades continue to need both optical and copper paths, a component-layer supplier like MACOM can capture some content in each speed transition, even if it does not present the same narrative intensity as pure module or end-platform vendors.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Current local sources do not prove that AI data center has become a dominant part of MACOM’s financial profile.
  • Current sources do not prove stable leadership share in 1.6T / 3.2T optical drivers or scale-up copper.
  • This page also does not prove revenue attribution across the broader optical catalog; it only confirms the direction and positioning of the named products.

docs.title: 2026-08-06 fiscal Q3 earnings update
docs.text:
• Fiscal Q3 revenue was USD 342.2M, up 35.8% year over year and 18.4% sequentially; adjusted operating margin was 31.5%.
  • Fiscal Q4 guidance was USD 415M-425M of revenue and adjusted EPS of USD 1.97-2.03.
  • The results move the enabling-components thesis from product-level relevance toward reported operating leverage, while company-level AI revenue attribution remains unclosed.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• 400G per lane optical-driver or scale-up copper products fail to convert into sustained design wins and production volume.
  • Interconnect roadmaps shift toward other component approaches or other suppliers, reducing MACOM’s content.
  • AI-relevant components remain present but too small inside the broader company to create a durable role upgrade.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
MTSI is the Active / Market-found spine 4 enabling-components name. The component positioning is real, but current local evidence is still closer to product-level fit than to a fully financially amplified core thesis.

Current action is routed only by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; MTSI is currently none, with no fallback.

docs.title: MU — Micron Technology
docs.text: Role: spine 3 HBM / DRAM / NAND physical-memory anchor Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-03-18; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Micron earns from DRAM, HBM, and NAND shipments. AI training/inference raises memory bandwidth and capacity demand; HBM increases value per bit, but memory remains highly cyclical. Record revenue, margin, and FCF prove monetization while increasing cycle-reversal risk.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: MU primary-owns the physical-memory/HBM node in Memory, Storage, and In-System Data Movement. Accelerator architecture belongs to Semiconductors and Foundational Compute, and manufacturing/package realization to Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. Enterprise data/context platforms such as SNOW remain in spine 9, not physical storage.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Accelerator/server platforms use more HBM/DRAM/NAND bits and higher-value mix. Micron monetizes volume, ASP, share, and product mix. Pricing, yield, HBM share, capex, and supply discipline determine profit; shortage can amplify returns and trigger the next supply cycle.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• FQ2 FY2026 revenue was USD 23.860B, versus USD 13.643B in FQ1 and USD 8.053B a year earlier.
  • GAAP/non-GAAP gross margin was 74.4%/74.9%; adjusted FCF was USD 6.899B.
  • Cloud Memory BU revenue was USD 7.749B; Core Data Center BU revenue was USD 5.687B.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: FQ3 guidance was revenue USD 33.5B ± 0.75B and gross margin near 81%; management calls memory strategic in the AI era. Pricing, shipments, and cash must validate the guide.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: HBM bandwidth and package complexity can make memory value per accelerator much higher than conventional server configurations.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Record pricing/margin cannot be perpetually extrapolated. Cloud/Core Data Center is not wholly AI/HBM, and capex, competitor supply, or customer digestion can create a cycle peak.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• HBM share, yield, or qualification lags and premium mix weakens.
  • DRAM/NAND supply outruns demand, collapsing ASP and gross margin.
  • Customer inventory or accelerator delivery enters a digestion period.
  • Capex rises while FCF and ROIC deteriorate materially through the cycle.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: MU is the Core / Market-found physical-memory anchor. HBM is proven rather than hidden; historical market-action overlays do not belong on this page.

docs.title: MXL MaxLinear
docs.text:
Role: spine 4 optical DSP / signal-chain modifier Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Modifier: former-half-hidden Evidence through: 2026-08-05

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects AI Optical Interconnect and DCI Hidden Treasure Monitoring Metrics Ledger as MXL's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: MaxLinear earns from broadband connectivity chips and high-speed interconnect chips. Its AI relevance comes from Keystone 400G/800G DSPs, AEC adjacency, and the Rushmore/Washington path into 1.6T optical/copper interconnect, but AI revenue and customers are still not disclosed separately.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: MXL primary-owns the optical DSP / high-speed signal-chain node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI. It is not a module OEM, switch vendor, or cloud operator; external manufacturing and packaging execution still belong in Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Module vendors, cable vendors, and data-center interconnect customers buy Keystone, Washington, and related parts, creating optical DSP, TIA, and AEC revenue. If hyperscale scale-up / scale-out programs keep entering production ramps, infrastructure revenue should show up first in company results. Real AI monetization still depends on product revenue splits, customer proof, and profit improvement, not the roadmap alone.

docs.title: 2026-07-23 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2026 revenue was USD 168.847M, up 23% sequentially and 55% year over year. Infrastructure revenue was USD 85.016M, or 50% of total revenue, up 145% year over year.
  • Non-GAAP gross margin was 59.5%, non-GAAP operating margin was 22.3%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS was USD 0.35; GAAP operating margin was (2.5)% and GAAP diluted EPS was USD 0.02.
  • Q3 guidance was revenue of USD 210M-220M and non-GAAP gross margin of 58.5%-61.5%. Named customer revenue, Keystone revenue dollars, and backlog remain undisclosed.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2026 revenue was USD 137.188M, up about 43%.
  • Management said infrastructure revenue grew >130%, and the later source refresh restated that as +136%.
  • The company tied growth to production ramps of optical data-center products at multiple hyperscale customers.
  • Keystone is defined as a 400G/800G PAM4 DSP; OFC 2026 materials said it has been adopted by module vendors and hyperscale data-center customers, with millions of units shipped.
  • Rushmore was launched as a 1.6T PAM4 DSP family for AI/ML and data-center networks, and Washington was launched as a 200G/lane TIA for 1.6T optical transceiver modules.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2026 revenue guide was USD 160M-170M, midpoint USD 165M.
  • Management described Q1 as the start of a multi-year growth phase driven by optical data-center connectivity.
  • The company frames Keystone volume production, Rushmore sampling, Washington availability, and Makalu 3.2T retimer sampling as the next-stage narrative.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If Keystone adoption keeps converting into revenue and profit, MXL fits better as a small-base optical DSP / signal-chain modifier than as a legacy broadband/connectivity cycle name.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Named hyperscaler revenue is not proven.
  • Keystone revenue dollars, customer count, and backlog are not proven.
  • Rushmore / Washington material revenue is not proven.
  • Silicon Motion dispute risk is not proven to be substantially resolved.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Silicon Motion arbitration turns materially adverse and absorbs the operating repair.
  • Infrastructure growth stalls and Keystone / Washington / Rushmore fail to convert into revenue or profit improvement.
  • The company cannot produce any durable AI / data-center revenue bridge and customer concentration stays high.
  • Competitors displace MaxLinear in optical DSP, AEC, or 1.6T signal-chain adoption.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: MXL is an Active / Market-found interconnect modifier. The old “half-hidden” label is no longer accurate, but this page still does not equate product presence with proven AI revenue quality.

docs.title: MYCR — Mycronic
docs.text:
Trading basis: Nasdaq Stockholm ordinary share; SEK; TradingView OMXSTO:MYCR Role: precision die bonding / photonic interconnect equipment; not an optical-module or CPO pure play Evidence through: 2026-08-05

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects MYCR, FN, and FORM AI Optical Manufacturing Current-Live Deep Dive and TV Execution Zones as MYCR's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: Bottom line
docs.text: Mycronic is a high-margin precision-equipment group. Its MRSI die-bonding tools directly address the sub-micron placement, flip-chip, eutectic/epoxy bonding, and wafer-level processes that are difficult to automate in optical-module and silicon-photonics volume production. Vanguard Automation adds photonic wire bonding. Standalone revenue, customers, and profit for the optical businesses remain unquantified, so the correct framing is optics optionality inside the group, not a proven CPO pure play.

docs.title: Position in the chain and boundaries
docs.text:
• MRSI belongs to Global Technologies / Die Bonding, not PCB Assembly Solutions / former High Flex.
  • High Volume is a separate adjacency: AI-server thermal dispensing and optical-module dispensing/final assembly.
  • Vanguard / Photonic Interconnects can use 3D nano-printing to create low-loss optical connections at specific interfaces. It does not replace die attach, all fibre coupling, thermal/electrical interconnects, reliability, or testing.
  • MRSI-LEAP's <±1 µm at 3σ, >1,000 UPH, and 24/7 targets prove equipment capability, not customer qualification, sole-source status, yield, or CPO revenue.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
AI optics complexity → tighter die-placement / bonding tolerance → die-bonder demand → customer qualification / tool shipment → GT revenue and margin

The issuer has shown strong optical-communications demand for die bonders and new optical-module final-assembly opportunities in High Volume. What remains missing is a bridge from aggregate Global Technologies / High Volume data to MRSI optics, Vanguard, and CPO orders → shipments → revenue → margin.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• H1 2026 group orders were SEK 5,446M, up 61%; sales were SEK 4,919M, up 17%; EBIT margin was 33.2%.
  • Global Technologies H1 orders were SEK 2,026M, sales SEK 1,195M, and EBIT margin 30.9%; the issuer explicitly reported strong optical-communications demand for die bonders.
  • MRSI-LEAP explicitly covers AI optical modules, silicon photonics, flip-chip, UV epoxy, and wafer-level packaging.
  • Mycronic acquired Vanguard Automation on 2024-04-01; Vanguard's 2023 sales were EUR 5.2M.
  • A 2025 issuer feature still described Vanguard's customers as mainly research and innovation centres.

docs.title: Cannot be extrapolated
docs.text:
• All Global Technologies / High Volume revenue is not optics revenue.
  • The group's H1 33.2% margin cannot be assigned directly to MRSI economics; Pattern Generators contributed about 80% of H1 divisional EBIT.
  • Management explicitly described the customized SLX as a one-off, with delivery only in 2028; it cannot justify mechanically annualizing H1 EPS.
  • A product-scale photonic-wire-bonding claim is not volume-customer qualification.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Standalone revenue, orders, backlog, customers, installed base, yield, ASP, or margin for MRSI optics, Vanguard, or CPO.
  • The scale at which Vanguard customers have moved from research/innovation centres to qualified volume manufacturers.
  • Whether High Volume optical-module final assembly produces recurring orders and sustainable margins.

docs.title: Financial and valuation facts
docs.text:
Net cash was SEK 2,267M on 2026-06-30. The normalized bridge uses about SEK 9,250M of sales, a trailing 23.85% EBIT margin, and roughly SEK 8.78 of normalized EPS; it does not simply double the favorable H1 Pattern Generators mix.

The 2026-08-04 regular-session price was SEK 324.40, about 36.9x normalized P/E, with a standard year-to-date return of +45.31%; these are dated market observations, not an instruction.

docs.title: Key risks / kill criteria
docs.text:
• Global Technologies order growth comes mainly from non-optics businesses, while the optical sub-chain remains unquantified.
  • Vanguard remains concentrated in research/innovation-centre customers.
  • Pattern Generators mix/backlog normalizes and group earnings fall materially below the current bridge.
  • FX, working capital, or acquisition/intangible risks weaken cash conversion.
  • The share price advances faster than the evidence.

docs.title: NET — Cloudflare
docs.text: Role: spine 9 edge / security / developer / AI delivery platform Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Unified ledger: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Cloudflare makes money from edge network, security, Zero Trust, developer-platform, and application-delivery subscriptions and usage. Its spine-9 role is enabling lower-latency deployment, delivery, and protection for APIs, applications, agents, and AI inference traffic, not owning hyperscaler capacity, E6 systems integration, or physical infrastructure.

docs.title: 2026-08-06 Q2 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q2 revenue was USD 696.1M, up 36% year over year, and current RPO grew 35%.
  • GAAP operating loss was USD 205.7M, or 29.6% of revenue, while non-GAAP operating income was USD 96.1M, or 13.8% of revenue.
  • FY2026 revenue outlook was USD 2.864B-2.870B. AI/Workers paid-revenue attribution remains undisclosed, and no Q&A transcript was captured.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: NET primary-owns the edge / security / developer delivery surface in AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle, while remaining adjacent to developer distribution in Platform Technology, Internet, and Distribution. It is not an application/data owner, does not primary-own E2 silicon or E6 systems, and does not own E7/E8 physical infrastructure. The failure point it controls is edge delivery, API protection, and network security for AI apps and agent runtime.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Revenue appears only when customers place AI apps, agents, APIs, and inference traffic on the edge runtime or network-security layer, driving Workers, delivery, security, and Zero Trust services. AI becomes revenue through usage, attach, and developer adoption. Broad network traffic, broad revenue, or total RPO do not automatically equal AI delivery revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 revenue was USD 639.8M, up 34% year over year.
  • Current RPO growth was 34%.
  • Non-GAAP operating income was USD 73.1M; GAAP operating loss was USD 62.0M.
  • The local 2026-06-28 SEC latest-route packet shows that subsequent locally visible filings were mainly DEFA14A, Form 4, and 144 routes, with no newer operating print added to this page's source set.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • Management describes AI as a fundamental re-platforming of the Internet and one of the company's major tailwinds.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If AI apps require lower-latency delivery, more API protection, more developer runtime, and tighter bot/agent security, Cloudflare's edge platform can expand attach and usage.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The company does not separately disclose AI revenue. Broad revenue, RPO, or edge traffic are not automatically AI delivery monetization.
  • "AI is re-platforming the Internet" still needs more specific Workers / AI / security adoption and economics proof before it can be treated as a separate AI revenue line.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: NET captures value through edge delivery, developer surface, and security attach, not by becoming an alternative hyperscaler, server owner, or facility-infrastructure beneficiary. The easiest misread is to write all AI network traffic as Cloudflare revenue, or to blur the developer edge platform into application/data ownership.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI-related usage stays mostly narrative, without clearer attach, retention, or revenue proof.
  • Hyperscaler, CDN, SASE, and developer-platform competition compress pricing or attach rates.
  • Developer/runtime adoption expands while GAAP losses and unit economics do not improve.
  • Edge/security demand grows without translating into a higher-quality recurring-revenue mix.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
NET is a Core / Market-found spine-9 edge / security / developer / AI delivery platform.

Current action is routed only by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; NET is currently none, with no fallback.

docs.title: NOK — Nokia Oyj
docs.text: Role: spine 4 IP / optical connectivity context Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Needs-source Evidence through: 2026-06-05; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Nokia earns from platform-scale network businesses across Network Infrastructure, Mobile Networks, and Cloud and Network Services. Its AI relevance mainly comes through optical, IP, data-center networking, and the Infinera addition, but this page remains context because the company-level AI / cloud story is not yet split into stable enough product-level revenue proof.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Nokia primary-owns the IP / optical connectivity large-platform node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI. It is not a pure switch vendor, pure optical-module vendor, or single data-center silicon name; mobile, fixed, and broader telecom mix still dilute the primary lane.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: When AI / cloud customers buy optical line systems, pluggables, IP routing, data-center switching, and intra-data-center optics, the revenue should first appear inside Network Infrastructure, Optical Networks, and IP Networks. To write this as a stronger thesis, the page still needs more stable product-level or customer-level revenue bridges.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• In Q1 FY2026, AI & Cloud customer net sales grew 49% and were 8% of group sales.
  • Nokia booked EUR 1B of AI & Cloud customer orders in the quarter.
  • In the same quarter, Network Infrastructure net sales grew 6%, including 20% growth in Optical Networks.
  • The official data-center networking page explicitly places high-performance switches, optics, and IP / optical interconnect inside data centers and to / from / between data centers, including 800GE and intra-data-center optics.
  • Nokia says the Infinera deal expands webscale exposure; official materials state that webscale / ICP customers were over 30% of Infinera sales and that Infinera had been developing high-speed, low-power intra-data-center optical components suited to AI workloads.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management raised the 2026 Network Infrastructure growth assumption to 12%-14% and the Optical + IP Networks growth assumption to 18%-20%.
  • Nokia raised its 2025-2028 AI & Cloud addressable-market CAGR assumption to 27%.
  • New DSP / optical solution timing from OFC remains product and volume-roadmap language that still needs follow-through.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Nokia has real AI / cloud optical and IP exposure, but it still looks more like one growth pocket inside a large platform than a standalone pure AI interconnect asset.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• A durable revenue split from AI / cloud into optical, IP, switching, or Infinera content is not proven.
  • It is not proven that AI / cloud orders are already converting into a structurally better profit mix.
  • It is not proven that the AI optical / IP story can outweigh legacy mobile / fixed / telecom cycle noise.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI & Cloud orders fail to keep converting into revenue or margin.
  • Optical / IP growth gets offset by weakness in other large segments.
  • Infinera integration, R&D burden, or execution complexity erodes returns.
  • Data-center networking products fail to win durable share and the AI exposure falls back to concept-level relevance.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: NOK is a Context / Needs-source large-platform IP / optical connectivity reference name. It helps explain the mainline, but current proof is still too broad to support a stronger pure AI interconnect conclusion.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: ServiceNow turns deployed compute into enterprise workflow and system-of-action platform revenue. The real test is not the model itself but whether AI moves from answering questions into governed workflow execution and then into durable ACV, subscription, and RPO growth.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: E9 AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle workflow / platform AI owner, centered on ITSM, CSM, HR, and enterprise-operations governed execution.
  • Boundary: it owns workflow, approval, ticket, and orchestration layers. It does not own E2 compute silicon, E6 systems manufacturing/integration, or any E7/E8 power and facility layer.
  • Distinction: NOW owns the workflow-execution control point. It is not CRM's customer-data control plane and not hyperscale cloud infrastructure.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• The core platform subscription base still carries the main seat and workflow revenue.
  • Now Assist, Context Engine, Autonomous Workforce, and Build Agent Skills can expand contract value if they increase attach and net-new ACV.
  • cRPO and RPO show future contract conversion, but broad subscription growth, cRPO, and total revenue are not direct AI revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2026 subscription revenue was USD 3.671B, up 22%.
  • Q1 FY2026 total revenue was USD 3.770B, up 22%.
  • cRPO was USD 12.64B, up 22.5%.
  • Total RPO was USD 27.7B, up 25%.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The count of Now Assist customers spending more than USD 1M in annual contract value grew more than 130% year over year.
  • There were 16 net-new ACV transactions above USD 5M, nearly +80% year over year.
  • Context Engine, Autonomous Workforce, Build Agent Skills, and EmployeeWorks were all named directly in the Q1 issuer packet.
  • FY2026 subscription-revenue guidance includes about 125 bps of Armis contribution and management-expected operating-margin and FCF-margin headwinds. This is forward comparability framing, not a realized result.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• NOW sits at the workflow-execution and governance node, so it has one of the cleanest paths to turn enterprise AI from assistant behavior into governed action.
  • If more cross-system workflows consolidate on NOW, AI can expand platform spend rather than just add a feature to existing seats.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• There is still no CRM-like direct AI ARR disclosure for NOW.
  • Broad subscription revenue, cRPO, and RPO are not directly attributable AI revenue.

docs.title: NVDA — NVIDIA
docs.text: Role: spine 2 accelerator platform / system architecture Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-26

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: NVIDIA earns from GPUs/accelerators, networking, systems, and enterprise software licenses/subscriptions. Its moat is the combined CUDA, interconnect, system design, and release cadence—not one GPU. AI workloads first become compute/networking shipments; mix, pricing, and software attach determine profit and cash.

docs.title: 2026-08-26 Q2 FY2027 update
docs.text:
• Revenue was USD 96.221B and Data Center revenue USD 89.0B, up 117% year over year. Q3 revenue guidance was USD 108B +/-2% without assuming China Data Center compute revenue.
  • Supply and capacity commitments were USD 279B, total future commitments USD 366B, total maximum guarantee exposure USD 108.5B, accounts receivable USD 63.1B with DSO of 60 days, inventory USD 31.6B, and Q2 senior-note issuance USD 25.0B.
  • The release advances demand and platform-execution proof while expanding the capital-intensity, customer-financing, receivable, inventory, and guarantee evidence to monitor.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: NVDA primary-owns the accelerator platform in Semiconductors and Foundational Compute. HBM belongs to Memory, Storage, and In-System Data Movement, wafer/package realization to Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials, and rack manufacturing to Systems, Racks, and Complex Manufacturing. These dependencies do not belong inside NVIDIA's primary lane.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Cloud, enterprise, and sovereign customers buy GPU, NVLink/NVSwitch, networking, and systems. Platform value comes from system ASP, software/services, iteration speed, and switching cost. Returns still depend on supply, gross margin, cash conversion, and installed-base utilization.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2027 revenue was USD 81.6B, up 85%; Data Center revenue was USD 75.2B, up 92%.
  • Data Center compute revenue was USD 60.4B, up 77%; networking revenue was USD 14.8B, up 199%.
  • GAAP/non-GAAP gross margin was about 74.9%/75.0%, showing strong current value capture.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: NVIDIA attributes future growth to agentic/physical AI, AI factories, and expansion beyond hyperscale. This forward claim needs later revenue-mix proof.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Software, interconnect, and systems integration raise switching costs and let NVIDIA capture more than single-chip value.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Current growth and margin cannot be perpetually extrapolated. Not all hyperscaler capex becomes NVIDIA revenue, and custom silicon, export controls, or supply shifts can change share and pricing.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Data Center growth, gross margin, or networking attach slows materially for several periods.
  • Large customers increase custom silicon and weaken accelerator share or bargaining power.
  • Export limits, advanced packaging/HBM supply, or system delivery blocks recognized revenue.
  • Competing platforms close the software/system total-cost gap.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
NVDA is the Core / Market-found compute-platform anchor. The market already recognizes its AI role.
