docs.title: NVT — nVent
docs.text: Role: Phase 5 E8 spine 8 site electrical boundary to energized rack; NVT is the enclosures / connectivity / liquid-cooling / power-distribution benchmark Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-05-01; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: nVent sits closer than ETN to the rack-adjacent mix of enclosures, power connections, control buildings, and cooling. It is not a generation owner or a server owner. In E8 it is the benchmark for rack-entry electrical / cooling exposure.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: NVT covers the inside-the-fence electrical and room-entry layer: cable management, control buildings, liquid / air cooling, electrical connections, enclosures, equipment protection, power connections, bus systems, switchgear systems, and power distribution solutions. It does not own upstream generation / fuel, and it does not own E6 servers / network systems.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As AI data-center density rises, rack-adjacent demand also rises for enclosures, power connections, busway, control buildings, PDU support, liquid-cooling support, and mission-critical protection. NVT monetizes AI by helping deliver power and thermal management safely to the rack rather than by selling compute.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The annual report and Q1 2026 10-Q state that nVent's portfolio includes cable management, control buildings, liquid / air cooling, electrical connections, enclosures, equipment protection, power connections, and power management solutions.
  • Systems Protection is defined as serving mission-critical applications including data centers and includes custom enclosures, liquid / air cooling, control buildings, switchgear systems, and power distribution solutions.
  • The Electrical Products Group acquisition is described as infrastructure solutions primarily for power utilities and data centers, operated mainly within Systems Protection.
  • The SC25 issuer product capture shows nVent actively selling a liquid-cooling and power portfolio into data-center and networking infrastructure.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• nVent describes itself as an enclosures and liquid-cooling leader and explicitly targets data-center / networking infrastructure as an application lane.
  • Company-wide backlog increased from USD 749.3M at year-end 2024 to USD 2.3499B at year-end 2025; management attributed the increase mainly to the Electrical Products Group acquisition and growth in the data-centers business and expected most backlog to ship in 2026. That company-wide total is not AI-backlog proof.
  • Q1 2026 disclosed USD 75.8M of acquired customer backlog with an estimated useful life of about three years, showing management tracks acquired backlog conversion, but that still does not equal fully closed organic AI monetization.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• Within E8, NVT is a more focused benchmark than ETN for rack-entry electrical / cooling because it directly covers the enclosure, connection, power-distribution, and liquid-cooling stack.
  • Backlog growth still reflects both acquisition and data-center growth, so the stronger evidence should not be translated mechanically into all-organic AI upside.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current raw packet still does not provide clean hyperscaler / data-center revenue share, organic backlog-growth split, or standalone margin disclosure for liquid cooling / power distribution.
  • former-half-hidden remains only a workflow modifier and should not be treated as a formal state or as a hidden-thesis conclusion.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If backlog growth remains mostly acquisition-driven without clearer organic data-center conversion, NVT's AI beneficiary profile is being overstated.
  • If the enclosure / connectivity / liquid-cooling offering does not translate into clearer customer, revenue, or margin proof, the benchmark role should remain context-only.
  • If data-center spend cools and NVT cannot prove durable attach rates for rack-entry electrical / cooling, the current positioning should not be upgraded.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: NVT is the Context / Market-found enclosures / connectivity / liquid-cooling / power-distribution benchmark in E8. former-half-hidden remains only a workflow modifier, not a formal discovery state.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Navitas belongs here as E8 high-voltage power semiconductor context: the local packet proves it has GaN/SiC products and high-voltage reference paths relevant to AI facility and rack power, but it does not support treating Navitas as an owner of E7 generation, E2 compute silicon, or E6 systems, and it does not close AI revenue into a durable investment judgment.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Navitas sits at the high-voltage power-semiconductor layer on the facility / rack-power side of the stack. The local evidence supports roles in GaN/SiC, 400V DC data-center power, and 800V-to-50V / 800V-to-6V reference paths; it does not support claiming ownership of generation assets, GPU/ASIC compute silicon, or complete systems.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: The revenue chain only closes if AI facilities or racks adopt higher-voltage DC architectures, Navitas parts or reference paths are actually designed into the PSU, PDB, or DC-DC stages, and those design-ins convert into recurring production shipments. The current local sources mostly prove product capability, reference paths, and ecosystem positioning, not direct AI revenue capture.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text: Company product material, SEC filings, and local raw captures prove that Navitas has high-power GaN/SiC products and has published 400V DC AI data-center material, a 10kW 800V DC-DC platform, and related 800V-to-50V / 800V-to-6V reference demonstrations.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Issuer-led material places those platforms inside the AI data-center and rack-power upgrade story, including 800 VDC / MGX ecosystem showcase language; that is issuer or ecosystem positioning, not proof of a purchase agreement, production order, or closed revenue attribution.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If AI facilities and racks keep moving toward 400V/800V HVDC and Navitas parts make it into production BOMs, it can benefit as an E8 high-voltage power-semiconductor supplier. That remains facility / rack-power context, not ownership of the broader AI power stack.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: The local packet does not yet close named hyperscaler or OEM production volume, AI revenue mix, durable BOM share, or sustained AI-driven margin improvement.

docs.title: 2026-08-07 Q2 official update

docs.title: Proven

docs.title: 2026-08-06 Q2 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q2 revenue was USD 343.1M, up 35.3% year over year and nearly 18% sequentially.
  • Advanced Nodes revenue grew 50% sequentially to a record, while Specialty Devices and Advanced Packaging reached an all-time high, supported by 2.5D logic, HBM, and silicon-photonics demand.
  • Backlog exceeded USD 1B for the first time. The company-wide AI revenue ratio, customer/order concentration, and valuation remain unclosed.

docs.title: Business and lane position
docs.text: Onto defines itself in the issuer raw as a process-control leader spanning 3D metrology, macro defect inspection, factory analytics, and advanced semiconductor packaging. For spine 5, its key ownership is not broad semiconductor capex but the process-control / metrology node inside HBM, fan-out, and 2.5D advanced packaging.

docs.title: AI to revenue
docs.text: The AI transmission has reached order / VPA and qualification evidence. In fiscal 2025, revenue was $1.0053 billion, and the company disclosed a new Dragonfly volume purchase agreement worth more than $240 million with a leading HBM manufacturer for 2D inspection and 3D bump metrology supporting expansion through 2027. It later disclosed Dragonfly G5 qualification for 2.5D AI packaging. The cleaner framing is that AI / HBM / advanced packaging have entered product orders and platform validation, while the local raw still does not provide a company-wide AI revenue ratio.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Fiscal 2025 revenue reached $1.0053 billion, and fourth-quarter revenue was $267 million.
  • The company disclosed a new volume purchase agreement worth more than $240 million with a leading HBM manufacturer for Dragonfly 2D inspection and 3D bump metrology supporting expansion through 2027.
  • Dragonfly G5 was qualified for 2.5D AI packaging.
  • The company defines itself as an advanced-packaging-related process-control supplier spanning wafer and package inspection / metrology.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management said global AI investment is driving a strong upcycle in semiconductor capital-equipment spending.
  • Initial Dragonfly G5 shipments are expected to begin in June 2026, and Dragonfly platform revenue is expected to grow more than 50% in 2026 versus 2025.
  • The early first-quarter preliminary revenue and second-quarter guidance are dated preliminary disclosures; the August 6 Q2 actual revenue of USD 343.1M supersedes that prior Q2 forecast.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: • Rising HBM, chiplet, fan-out, and 2.5D / 3D packaging complexity should increase package-level inspection and metrology content and sensitivity requirements.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Company-wide AI revenue share.
  • AI demand is already strong enough to create durable margin expansion; 2025 operating margin was still below the prior year.

docs.title: Company kill criteria

docs.title: ORCL — Oracle
docs.text: Role: spine 1 demand / capacity economics Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-20

docs.title: 2026-08-20 evidence refresh — demand is real; conversion remains the question
docs.text:
• FY2026 Q4 RPO reached USD 638B, up USD 85B sequentially; Q4 OCI/IaaS revenue was USD 5.787B (+93% year over year), while FY2026 OCI/IaaS revenue was USD 18.101B (+77%).
  • The same FY2026 evidence records USD 55.663B capex, USD 31.977B operating cash flow, and USD -23.686B FCF, alongside USD 129.541B borrowings, USD 31.894B cash/securities, major lease commitments, and future financing plans. Demand strength therefore does not close the capital, delivery, margin, or per-share conversion question.
  • RPO is staged contracted revenue, not an energized-capacity, utilization, supplier-allocation, or margin guarantee. About USD 75B of large-AI-contract RPO reflects customer-prepaid or customer-supplied GPU hardware and must not be relabeled as Oracle-funded supplier demand.
  • The 2026-08-20 market-valuation correction（源文件保留在私有研究库） replaces only the older OHLCV table. The accepted 2026-08-19 USD 143.81 close and valuation sensitivity remain unchanged; the dated market snapshot remains evidence context only.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Oracle earns subscription and usage revenue from databases, enterprise applications, and OCI. Its AI-chain role is not making chips, power, or facility equipment; it converts long-duration cloud contracts into capacity that must be delivered. The central test is whether RPO becomes capacity, revenue, margin, and cash on schedule.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Oracle is a demand anchor in Cloud and Compute Demand. It buys GPU, network, storage, land, power, and facility delivery for enterprise and AI customers. Unlike suppliers such as NVDA, VRT, or BE, Oracle operates the capacity; its capex alone does not prove any supplier's revenue attribution.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: OCI, database, and application contracts first enter RPO. Revenue is recognized as Oracle delivers capacity and services. AI raises compute usage and campus intensity, but value capture depends on delivery speed, contract mix, pricing, financing cost, and post-capex cash conversion.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• FY2026 Q4 RPO was USD 638B, up 363% year over year and USD 85B sequentially.
  • Q4 OCI/IaaS revenue was USD 5.787B, up 93% year over year; FY2026 OCI/IaaS revenue was USD 18.101B, up 77%.
  • FY2026 capex was USD 55.663B, FCF was USD -23.686B, borrowings were USD 129.541B, and cash/securities were USD 31.894B.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • FY2027 revenue guidance is USD 90B, and the company expects additional debt/equity financing; both remain forward guidance rather than reported results.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Contracted demand at this scale can support power, facility, interconnect, cooling, and storage procurement. Supplier share, timing, and margin still require company-specific order evidence.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: RPO is not all AI, near-term, or high-margin revenue. Capex does not automatically improve FCF or identify a particular equipment beneficiary.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: Oracle's advantage is its database/application installed base, multicloud connections, and large OCI contracts. The market already sees the demand; the open question is RPO conversion, capacity delivery, and financed returns.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• RPO grows while IaaS revenue conversion keeps slowing.
  • Capex and financing rise without improvement in operating margin, FCF, or leverage.
  • Power, GPU, network, or construction delays block contracted capacity.
  • Large contracts are renegotiated, cancelled, or carry poor pricing/mix.

docs.text:
ORCL is a Core / Market-found demand entity and capex-spillover validator.

Current action is routed only by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; ORCL is currently none, with no fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: PDD's stable position is a China ecommerce and Temu cross-border commerce platform. Recommendation, advertising, and algorithmic capabilities matter, but this is first a commerce-platform owner, not an AI-revenue owner and not a finance, application-software, or infrastructure owner.

docs.text: PDD sits on the platform-tech / internet side of E10 cross-theme portfolio prose. Its stable ownership is the China ecommerce and Temu platform. It does not absorb the finance-owner roles of UPST, PGY, or KLAR, and it does not turn recommendation, advertising, or merchant tooling into an independent application or infrastructure owner.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: PDD's AI relevance mainly comes from recommendation, advertising distribution, search ranking, and merchant / consumer matching efficiency, but those technologies are a secondary mechanism rather than the page's primary ownership. FY2025 reported revenue and profit prove commerce scale, but broad commerce totals are not AI revenue. Merchant, advertising, or transaction totals do not automatically equal AI proof.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The local source manifest and FY2025 SEC 6-K provide issuer / SEC-level evidence for the ecommerce and platform business.
  • The PDD and Temu business frame can be written durably as a China ecommerce / cross-border commerce platform rather than a peripheral sample.
  • Q2 2026 revenue was RMB 112.4B, up 8%; operating profit was RMB 27.8B, up 8%; OCF was RMB 25.7B; cash and short-term investments were RMB 456.4B.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The local SEC / issuer evidence supports value capture through the merchant, consumer, and transaction-fulfillment network.
  • That framing proves commerce-platform positioning, but it does not by itself prove recommendation or advertising technology as separated AI revenue.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If the platform keeps improving matching efficiency, user retention, and merchant productivity, technology investment should keep serving commerce economics.
  • That technology value belongs first to ecommerce-platform execution, not to an independent AI-software owner.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local source set does not isolate AI revenue.
  • Broad GMV, revenue, advertising, or merchant totals are not automatic proof of AI monetization.

docs.title: Value capture and boundary of misread
docs.text: PDD captures value by turning traffic distribution, transaction matching, fulfillment, and cross-border platform capability into a scaled commerce engine. The misread boundary is treating broad commerce totals as AI revenue, or expanding recommendation / advertising technology into an independent application or infrastructure owner. PDD owns the ecommerce / Temu platform role here, not a finance or AI-infrastructure role.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If commerce growth, merchant economics, or cross-border fulfillment pressure deteriorates, platform value capture gets hit first.
  • Q2 non-GAAP net income declined 13%, so cash richness does not establish growth or duration.
  • If regulation, cross-border policy, or platform-governance issues weaken Temu or PDD transaction efficiency, the E10 ownership should contract.
  • If later local issuer / SEC evidence still cannot separate technology capability from independent AI monetization, this page should keep refusing to rewrite broad commerce totals as AI revenue.

docs.text: PDD is Active / Market-found. Its stable ownership is the China ecommerce and Temu platform. Q2 remains profitable and cash-generative, but growth/earnings deceleration plus Temu/ADR/regulatory risk constrain conviction. Any current action lives only in China Tech Megacaps Six-Company Deep Dive Conclusion; this entity owns no bands and large position=NO.

docs.title: PDFS — PDF Solutions
docs.text: Role: spine 5 manufacturing / packaging / test / materials active; yield / process-control analytics data layer Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-06

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: PDF Solutions mainly sells the analytics, connectivity, and process-control software layer for fab + assembly + test. Its AI relevance comes from the data-management and yield-improvement complexity of advanced packaging and test, not from any physical-equipment node.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: PDFS primary-owns the yield / process-control analytics data layer inside Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. It is not a bonder, substrate supplier, inspection tool, or OSAT-capacity owner; it provides the software, connectivity, and analysis layer that stitches together fab, assembly, test, and backend equipment data.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As advanced packaging and test become more complex, data standardization, yield analysis, and process control become more valuable. PDFS's current revenue bridge comes from Exensio usage in Intel AP&T and OSAT settings, CIM300 backend connectivity, and a business scale already visible in Q1 2026 revenue, margins, and backlog.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 quarterly total revenues were $60.1m, up 26% YoY; GAAP gross margin was 72%, non-GAAP gross margin was 76%; GAAP operating margin was 10%, non-GAAP operating margin was 25%; ending backlog was $246.4m.
  • The Intel page is explicitly titled Leveraging PDF Exensio for Intel Advanced Packaging and Test and says advanced packaging / testing creates major data-standardization and analysis challenges; Intel uses Exensio to manage and analyze manufacturing data from wafer fabrication to final testing.
  • Exensio OSAT is explicitly for Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test companies and includes process control, test operations, and assembly operations.
  • Exensio platform text says it spans fabrication, testing, assembly, and enterprise processes and states 55,000+ fab tools connected, 40,000+ process tools under process control, and customers across 350 organizations / 20 countries.
  • CIM300 explicitly says GEM300 standards can be adopted on semiconductor backend equipment, including packaging assembly and test equipment, even when the substrate is not a wafer.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • The Intel use case, OSAT positioning, and platform-scale metrics all come from issuer / product-page language; they prove product presence and routing but not a separate advanced-packaging / test revenue split by themselves.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: PDFS is a beneficiary of advanced packaging / test yield and process-control analytics, but the page only stays clean if it keeps the “data layer, not physical equipment” boundary explicit. It currently looks former-half-hidden: no longer totally overlooked, but also not one of the most crowded first-line hardware bottlenecks.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AP&T / OSAT revenue mix is not separately disclosed.
  • Intel revenue contribution, customer concentration, and the share of backlog tied specifically to packaging / test are not disclosed.
  • It is not proven that PDFS should be written as a hardware bottleneck owner inside advanced packaging.

docs.title: 2026-08-06 Q2 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q2 revenue was USD 61.5M, up 19% year over year, and ending backlog was USD 270.7M.
  • Management reaffirmed its 20% annual revenue-growth target and cited secureWISE, DirectScan, and Exensio customer wins.
  • Platform revenue fell 4% sequentially, volume-based revenue rose 35% sequentially, capex was USD 14.1M, and the May secondary issued 1.9M shares.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Intel / OSAT use cases remain showcase references instead of scaling commercially.
  • Platform breadth and connected-tool scale stop translating into backlog, margins, or retention quality.
  • The market starts treating PDFS as an equipment play and the thesis boundary becomes distorted.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
PDFS is an Active / Market-found yield / process-control analytics name with a former-half-hidden workflow modifier. The key requirement is to preserve the boundary that this is an analytics data-layer name, not a physical-equipment name.

docs.text: Palantir turns deployed compute into enterprise and government operational deployment software revenue. docs.title: Lane and boundary

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• As enterprise and government customers expand software deployment across more use cases, users, and tasks, Palantir can convert that into larger platform contracts and revenue.
  • The acceleration in U.S. commercial and broader U.S. revenue shows that this path is real, but broad company growth is still not the same as standalone AI revenue.
  • The real test is deployment breadth, repeatability, and cross-customer replication, not treating all revenue as one single AI product bucket.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 revenue growth was +85% year over year.
  • U.S. revenue growth was +104% year over year.
  • U.S. commercial revenue growth was +133% year over year.
  • Rule of 40 score was 145%.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to about +71% growth.
  • The local source spine classifies PLTR as a software-platform name with hard AI evidence, not just concept narrative.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• PLTR sits at the operational landing layer after compute is already deployed, so enterprise and government rollout can continue absorbing platform spend once infrastructure is in place.
  • That makes it an E9 software-deployment owner rather than an infrastructure owner.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local evidence does not split out a standalone AI product-bucket revenue bridge or a finer commercial versus government AI revenue bridge.
  • Broad company growth, U.S. growth, and commercial growth are not all directly attributable AI revenue.
  • The current local packet also does not prove that this growth has already become broader, more diversified long-duration revenue quality.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If very high growth starts depending on a small set of large programs and cross-customer repeatability weakens, the E9 owner case should be downgraded.

  • If deployment quality weakens on either the commercial or government side, the broad AI software deployment thesis needs to be rewritten.

docs.text:
Updated: 2026-09-09

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for PLUG; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Plug Power sells fuel-cell systems, hydrogen supply, and related infrastructure capabilities. In this wiki it is not an ordinary data-center onsite-power company; it is a special case for whether hydrogen-product relevance can convert into data-center revenue before capital-structure stress overwhelms the path.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: the hydrogen-optionality branch of spine 7, Onsite Bridge Power, Storage, and Backup
  • Boundary: this page only covers generation products, fuel supply, and time-to-power realization constraints
  • It does not own site switchgear, rack power, cooling, EPC/MEP, or any spine-8 infrastructure delivery in Facility Electrical, Rack Power, Cooling, and Delivery

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Realized results: the local filing and product materials show that the company explicitly treats data-center power as an application path and has a corresponding high-power fuel-cell platform.
  • Forward path: the AI/data-center narrative reaches realization only if issuer disclosure converts that application path into named projects, repeat orders, verifiable revenue/backlog, and sustainable unit economics.
  • Current conclusion: the existing filing does not break data-center activity into auditable commercial results, and capital-structure pressure remains the dominant constraint.

docs.title: 2026-08-10 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 revenue was about USD 178M, and gross margin improved to approximately breakeven from about -31% a year earlier. Net cash usage was about USD 61M, down about 58% sequentially.
  • Cash and cash equivalents were about USD 162M; total cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash were USD 671.5M. The issuer raised FY2026 revenue-growth guidance to 15%-16% and reiterated a Q4 positive-EBITDAS target.
  • The subsequent USD 80M Graham/electricity-rights transaction is a liquidity event. It does not establish data-center recurring revenue, durable unit economics, or a resolved capital structure.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Filing / issuer-primary: the Q1 2026 Form 10-Q and FY2025 annual filing define the current disclosure boundary.
  • Product / commercial materials: the GenSure HP launch and electricity-rights monetization materials show the product path and asset actions behind the hydrogen-power narrative.
  • Conclusion: the evidence currently reaches application direction and product preparedness, not data-center commercial revenue with healthy economics.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Company materials identify data-center power as a target application and present platform and asset actions intended to support that path.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: That is enough to keep PLUG in the hydrogen / capital-structure special-situation bucket, but not enough to restore it to the ordinary onsite-power ranking.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Named data-center projects with realized revenue or backlog
  • Repeat-deployment economics, gross profit, or operating performance
  • A sustainable business path that no longer depends on recurring financing support

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later issuer evidence still stops at application language without data-center commercial realization, PLUG remains context-only and does not re-enter the ordinary ranking
  • If capital-structure or operating stress overwhelms product optionality to the point that the path is no longer realistically executable, it can leave ongoing spine-7 maintenance

docs.title: POWL — Powell Industries
docs.text: Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for POWL; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Powell owns medium-voltage switchgear and in-site power distribution within E8, taking power that has already reached the site and routing, protecting, and distributing it to critical loads inside the campus.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: POWL's primary lane is medium-voltage switchgear, site power distribution, power control rooms, e-houses, and integrated power packages. It is the owner of in-campus power distribution and control equipment; it does not own utility interconnection or substation EPC, it does not own rack-side UPS or thermal infrastructure, and it does not own upstream generation and fuel assets or server and networking-system manufacturing.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: After external power reaches an AI campus, it still has to be safely distributed to buildings, modules, and critical loads. Powell monetizes the layer where power is on site but not yet reliably distributed across the campus through switchgear, distribution systems, PCR and e-house products, and integrated power packages.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The Q1 FY2026 results raw file explicitly discloses data-center orders well in excess of USD 100M, including a megaproject booking of about USD 75M, proving the company has won real datacenter electrical-delivery demand.
  • The Integrated Package Solutions product page shows Powell is not just selling a single cabinet; it also offers power control rooms, e-houses, and more integrated in-site distribution solutions.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Company framing presents datacenter orders, integrated package solutions, and more complex electrical-delivery requirements as growth drivers.
  • The current local issuer and product evidence supports Powell's effort to expand through higher-spec electrical packaging, but that remains issuer framing rather than a disclosed long-duration AI revenue structure.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI campuses keep scaling in size and load density, the content per project for in-site medium-voltage distribution, protection, and modular electrical rooms should rise, making Powell's revenue bridge broader than standalone switchgear.
  • POWL is distinctive because it sits after the utility handoff and before rack and facility thermal infrastructure, owning the middle layer where in-site distribution actually has to get built.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local evidence does not show a durable revenue and margin conversion path from datacenter orders, and it does not prove that this order intensity will persist.
  • The current local evidence does not support Powell owning utility interconnection or substation EPC, or rack-side power and thermal infrastructure; those remain separate owners.

docs.title: Q3 FY2026 result — order proof upgraded, call pending
docs.text:
• The official release reported Q3 revenue of USD 312M / +9%, gross margin of 30.6%, and diluted EPS of USD 1.42; the upgrade is concentrated in the order and backlog evidence rather than an unqualified earnings beat.
  • New orders were USD 934M / +158%, about 3.0x book-to-bill, and backlog was USD 2.4B / +69%, including a data-center mega order above USD 400M. The order is tied to a behind-the-meter on-site-generation design, strengthening proof at the E8 site-distribution/custom-package layer.
  • The Q1 and Q3 SEC acceptance-time proxies both sit about 18.5 hours before the next-day 11:00 ET call. That is established after-close-release / next-morning-call cadence, not an unusual Q3 delay. SEC acceptance is a filing-time proxy, the issuer gave no scheduling rationale, and Q3 call/Q&A had not occurred at the 2026-08-04 14:39 CEST research cutoff.
  • The 2026-08-04 07:12 CEST Futu capture reported after-hours USD 188.2224, overnight USD 189.98, and bid/ask USD 188.10/189.00. These were thin extended-hours indications, recorded alongside the completed-session snapshot and the 200D 191.2044; they do not establish regular-session liquidity or delivery economics.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later disclosure shows datacenter orders are not converting into sustained in-site distribution revenue, or integrated packages are not increasing content per project, the E8 owner thesis weakens.
  • If execution remains too project-custom and value capture stays thin, Powell's stability inside E8 declines.
  • If the page starts extending Powell into utility-interconnection ownership, upstream generation and fuel ownership, or rack-thermal ownership without local-source support, that is a kill signal.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Role: Core / Market-found; modifier: former-half-hidden. Stable E8 owner for medium-voltage switchgear and site power distribution; not an E7 generation/fuel owner and not an E6 server or networking-system manufacturer.

docs.title: PSIX — Power Solutions International
docs.text: Updated: 2026-09-09 CEST Industry page: Onsite Bridge Power, Storage, and Backup

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Power Solutions International's core business is natural-gas / diesel gensets and power systems. It sells onsite generation and standby equipment, not utility-generation asset ownership.

docs.title: 2026-08-06 Q2 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q2 net sales were USD 152.5M, down 21% year over year, and diluted EPS was USD 0.73. The company attributed lower sales to Power Systems shipment timing and softer oil/gas demand.
  • Management said data-center power-solutions demand remains strong, reduced total debt by about USD 30.8M, and expects second-half sales to exceed first-half sales.
  • Order timing, data-center shipment conversion, and the durability of margin improvement remain open.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• It belongs to the Phase 5 E7 onsite / bridge generation and backup-equipment segment inside the generation / grid / time-to-power causal lane.
  • The role boundary stops at genset and power-systems supply. It does not extend into site electrical distribution, rack power, cooling, or EPC spine 8.
  • PSIX is a bridge / backup equipment mechanism, not a utility-generation owner and not a proven AI pure play.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If a data center, campus, or supporting utility needs power before permanent supply is fully ready, PSIX can turn that time-to-power need into revenue through gensets, power systems, and after-sales support. That path depends on orders, shipment timing, and project cadence; it is not a durable AI annuity by default.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The local power-systems capture explicitly lists DATA CENTER and UTILITY among the end markets.
  • Local results and call captures include direct management references to data-center demand or data-center applications.
  • The local 10-K capture is enough to establish that the company sells engines and power-systems equipment, not an abstract theme proxy.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company places data-center demand inside the demand stack for the power-systems business.
  • Company materials position PSIX as a supplier that can provide faster onsite or standby power capability.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• PSIX belongs on the active Phase 5 E7 list because the product mechanism clearly sits in the onsite / bridge generation and backup lane.
  • But this page is about a high-volatility equipment supplier, not about a proven owner of stable AI economics.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The page does not have named hyperscaler deployment evidence or repeatable data-center order proof.
  • The page does not isolate AI-only revenue, AI-only backlog, or data-center-only service revenue.
  • The page also does not prove that this revenue path is durable enough to classify PSIX as an AI pure play.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If future issuer-primary or filing evidence stops naming data centers as an end market or demand driver for power systems, this page's role should be downgraded.
  • If data-center-linked orders fail to turn into repeat shipments, revenue, or service evidence, the AI-to-revenue logic should be rewritten.
  • If the business mix shifts back toward generic industrial or oil-and-gas volatility rather than time-to-power / standby use cases, this page should leave mainline tracking.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
active; modifier: Needs-source, distressed-proof-first. Proof gates: 1. Issuer-primary or filing evidence for a named customer, project, or deployment scope. 2. Repeatable revenue, backlog, or aftermarket evidence tied to that scope. 3. Clear proof that data-center demand is a repeatable product path rather than a one-off order burst.

Current action is routed only by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; PSIX is currently none, with no fallback.

docs.title: Lane and boundary

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Before a rack can be energized, an AI campus has to solve interconnection, expansion, substation work, line work, and site electrical delivery. Quanta monetizes that layer through utility work, substation work, large-load-center electrical construction, and commissioning, with revenue conversion tied to project execution milestones rather than standalone equipment shipments.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The FY2025 10-K and the Q1 2026 10-Q explicitly cover electric power transmission and distribution, substations, and infrastructure services for large load centers including data centers and advanced manufacturing.
  • Company filings place data centers, technology-related dynamics, electrification, and utility demand in the same demand frame, proving Quanta already sits in the execution layer of AI-campus power delivery.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Issuer framing treats electric-infrastructure demand, large-load-center buildout, and related delivery work as future growth sources.
  • The local evidence supports management's view that datacenter demand and broader grid buildout are linked demand drivers, but that is still a workload and backlog framing rather than a disclosed AI revenue breakout.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If hyperscaler and colocation campuses need faster interconnection, substation expansion, and site delivery, an execution platform like PWR should benefit directly from higher engineering complexity and tighter schedules.
  • PWR's E8 role is to convert utility-side readiness into a deliverable site, not to own upstream power supply itself and not to own downstream equipment content.

docs.title: RMBS — Rambus
docs.text: Role: spine 3 memory-interface chips / controller IP / CXL Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Workflow modifier: former-half-hidden Evidence through: 2026-08-19; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger, whose memory/storage row is none with no fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Rambus earns from memory-interface chips, silicon-IP licensing, and contract revenue. It does not make HBM/DRAM; it supplies controllers, interfaces, and connectivity between processor and memory. Existing DDR5-related product revenue is financial, while HBM4E/CXL remains more forward-looking.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: RMBS primary-owns the interface/controller/IP node in Memory, Storage, and In-System Data Movement. MU owns physical memory and NVDA/AMD compute architecture. Rambus connects them without owning either. Enterprise data/context software remains in spine 9.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Higher bandwidth and channel count can raise interface-chip volume, content, and IP-license opportunities. Production products create product revenue; IP/design wins monetize through license, royalty, or contract. Standards, qualification, mix, and repeat wins determine value.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 GAAP revenue was USD 180.2M; product revenue was USD 88.0M, up 15%.
  • Licensing billings were USD 70.8M; operating cash flow was USD 83.2M.
  • Q2 FY2026 GAAP revenue was USD 207.385M; product revenue was USD 99.154M, royalties USD 84.261M, and licensing billings USD 84.1M.
  • Quarter-end Q2 AR was USD 144.094M and inventory USD 74.836M. The two largest customers represented 22% and 16% of Q2 revenue, and two customers represented 42% and 23% of quarter-end AR.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Rambus guided Q3 total/product revenue to USD 210-216M / USD 110-116M and explicitly conditioned achievement in part on signing customer agreements for product sales and solutions licensing. Public primary evidence through the cutoff does not establish that the Q3-required agreements were signed. That is publicly unproven, not a claim that they were not signed. LPDDR5X SOCAMM2, HBM4E controller IP, CXL, and PCIe 7 are product-direction evidence, not production share or attributable revenue.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: A tighter bandwidth bottleneck can increase controller/interface complexity and monetizable IP value, making Rambus closer to data movement than generic AI adjacency.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: HBM4E/CXL/PCIe optionality is not current revenue. Q3 agreement signing, named or quantified design wins, share, royalty rate, and production timing are not disclosed facts.

docs.title: 2026-08-19 Q2 10-Q follow-up
docs.text:
• Q2 actual delivery substantiates the product/royalty/billings engines, but the Q3 product outlook remains an agreement-dependent forward expectation. Guidance, product offering, or negotiations must not be relabeled as booked orders or revenue.
  • Cash quality remains open: 1H operating cash flow was USD 144.458M, below USD 171.773M a year earlier, while inventory increased from USD 44.098M at 2025 year-end. AR, inventory, and customer concentration must be revisited with Q3 actuals.
  • The 2026-08-18 regular close of USD 93.71 is a dated market-data fact only. It does not establish a valuation conclusion, current action, or numeric-zone authority.

docs.title: SANM Sanmina
docs.text: Evidence through: 2026-08-19; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger, whose systems/manufacturing row is none with no fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Sanmina is an electronics-manufacturing and complex-systems delivery company. For spine 6, the most relevant piece is the Communications Networks and Cloud & AI Infrastructure bucket together with the acquired ZT Systems manufacturing capability. Its official capability pages also cover optical/RF/microelectronics, PCB, backplane, cable, rack integration, and test.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: In spine 6, SANM is a manufacturing/integration exposure, with the most direct handle coming from ZT-enabled cloud-rack and cluster-scale AI manufacturing. It is not a branded systems vendor and must not be treated as a pure optical/DCI name. It belongs to the same manufacturing-conversion layer as CLS and FN, but customer and product boundaries differ.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2026 net sales were USD 4.013B; Communications Networks and Cloud and AI Infrastructure revenue was USD 2.771B, up about 278% year over year and about 69% of total sales.
  • For H1 FY2026, the same bucket generated USD 4.735B, up about 222% year over year. The 10-Q says the increase was primarily driven by the cloud-infrastructure end market, the ZT acquisition, new program wins, and related ramp-ups.
  • The Q2 FY2026 SEC/IR primary capture（源文件保留在私有研究库） records ZT Systems revenue of USD 1.88B, about 46.9% of quarterly revenue; it also lists product examples including 400G/800G/1.6T optical systems and pluggables, accelerated-compute GPU, storage, and IP switching/routing.
  • Q3 FY2026 net sales were USD 3.464016B. The reported combined Communications Networks and Cloud & AI Infrastructure end-market bucket was USD 2.148413B, or 62.02% of revenue. It is a combined bucket, not pure Cloud/AI revenue and not optical/DCI revenue.
  • The Q3 10-Q discloses ZT Systems revenue of about USD 1.1B in Q3 and about USD 4.0B since acquisition. Because ZT is integrated into ongoing operations, standalone profitability is not determinable.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2026 and H1 FY2026 revenue, growth, and mix for Communications Networks and Cloud and AI Infrastructure have been disclosed.
  • The 10-Q and issuer capture state that growth in this bucket was primarily driven by the cloud-infrastructure end market, the ZT acquisition, and new program wins.
  • Q3 combined end-market revenue, ZT revenue, and consolidated margin/cash flow have been disclosed; they do not provide standalone ZT margin, FCF, or optical revenue.
  • The AMD/ZT transaction materials state that Sanmina became AMD's preferred NPI manufacturing partner for cloud rack and cluster-scale AI solutions; ZT is described as a manufacturer of AI and general-purpose computer infrastructure for hyperscale computing companies.
  • Official capability pages support optical/RF/microelectronics, high-speed PCB/backplane/cable, rack integration, and test capability.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Product examples and capability pages show what Sanmina wants to serve, but capability descriptions are not standalone proof of revenue realization.
  • The preferred NPI manufacturing partner wording proves positioning in the relationship, not an automatic long-term large-scale revenue commitment.
  • Management said core Sanmina and ZT secured more customer orders, but it did not disclose order dollars, backlog, duration, named customers, acceptance milestones, or attributable revenue. This remains an issuer statement, not a quantified orders-to-revenue bridge.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• SANM's most credible AI monetization path is cloud-rack and cluster-scale manufacturing rather than a fully proven optical/DCI revenue story.
  • Optical, backplane, cable, and test capabilities show that SANM can participate in more complex networking/interconnect manufacturing content, but that eligibility cannot be written up as material optical revenue.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• That material AI optical/DCI revenue has formed a separately visible revenue pool.
  • Named hyperscaler, network-OEM, or optical-customer revenue beyond the AMD/ZT language.
  • Standalone ZT margin, FCF, cash-cycle contribution, or integration completion.
  • That optical/RF/microelectronics mix has been proven to sustain higher consolidated margins.

docs.title: 2026-08-19 Q3 10-Q follow-up
docs.text:
• The Q3 10-Q advances the ZT/cloud-rack manufacturing case from direction to revenue evidence, but the USD 2.148413B combined bucket cannot be renamed as pure AI or optical/DCI revenue. About USD 1.1B of ZT revenue is not a substitute for standalone profitability.
  • The customer-quality gate remains open: top-ten customers represented 62% of Q3 sales (67% for nine months); one customer represented at least 10% of Q3 revenue and one customer represented at least 10% of gross AR at quarter end.
  • The cash-quality gate remains open: Q3 OCF was USD 124.491M, net PP&E purchases USD 100.806M, and issuer-defined FCF USD 23.685M. Nine-month trade-receivable sales were USD 486.745M, limiting a simplistic OCF/FCF reading. Quarter-end cash was USD 1.844942B, total term debt USD 2.172310B, and Q3 interest expense USD 32.464M.
  • The 2026-08-18 regular close of USD 198.28 is a dated market-data fact only. It does not establish a valuation conclusion, current action, or numeric-zone authority.

docs.title: 2026-08-19 Q3 public-disclosure closure addendum
docs.text:
Source: SANM Q3 public-disclosure closure raw addendum（源文件保留在私有研究库）.

  • CLOSED: ZT revenue existence (about USD 1.1B in Q3 and USD 4.0B since acquisition), the top-ten concentration baseline (62% in Q3 and 67% for nine months), the combined-bucket negative classification, and the cancellation-protection negative boundary. The combined bucket is not pure Cloud/AI or optical/DCI revenue; cancellable bookings and customer material liability do not establish enforceable cancellation protection.
  • BLOCKED-PUBLIC-DISCLOSURE: the reviewed official public record does not provide ZT standalone margin/FCF/cash-cycle, quantified order dollars/backlog/duration, or optical/DCI attribution. This is a disclosure boundary, not a claim that the economics, orders, or optical/DCI program did not occur.
  • PARTIAL: official Q&A remains inaccessible; this closure obtained no official transcript, deck text, or audio and therefore makes no Q&A attribution or inference.
  • Authority is unchanged: systems/manufacturing registry=none, current action=none, numeric-zone authority=NO, and large position=NO; closure does not automatically upgrade any of those authorities. The routine next review is Q4 FY2026 results / the FY2026 10-K after the 2026-10-03 fiscal quarter end.

docs.title: 2026-08-20 Q3 issuer-deck follow-up
docs.text:
Source: SANM Q3 FY2026 issuer-deck follow-up（源文件保留在私有研究库）.

  • Deck text is now locally captured: core Sanmina revenue was USD 2.4B, ZT revenue was USD 1.1B, Q4 ZT outlook was USD 0.8B-1.0B, and FY2026 ZT outlook was USD 4.8B-5.0B for 11 months.
  • This is an evidence/source delta. It does not establish quantified orders/backlog/duration, named-customer economics, acceptance-to-revenue conversion, ZT standalone margin/FCF, or optical/DCI revenue attribution; the filed integrated-business boundary remains controlling.
  • Authority remains systems/manufacturing registry=none, current action=none, numeric-zone authority=NO, and large position=NO. SANM cannot inherit optics/DCI authority, and no HERMES or remote state changed.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Communications Networks and Cloud and AI Infrastructure growth falls back quickly after the ZT step-up, with no replacement programs.
  • ZT integration, customer concentration, debt/interest, or receivable-sales dependence worsens enough to impair manufacturing-conversion quality.
  • ZT revenue fails to turn into identifiable margin, FCF, and cash-cycle quality.
  • The AMD cloud-rack/cluster-scale NPI relationship does not translate into durable manufacturing programs.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Active / Market-found manufacturing/integration exposure in spine 6. The core case is not "a hidden optics name"; it is that ZT makes the AI/cloud-rack manufacturing evidence tangible, while the optical/interconnect piece remains at capability and product-category level. The unified ledger's systems/manufacturing row remains none, so SANM cannot inherit the optics/DCI page's authority: there is no current wiki action and no numeric-zone authority. docs.title: SMHN — SUSS MicroTec
docs.text: Role: spine 5 manufacturing / packaging / test / materials active; temporary bonding / debonding / hybrid bonding equipment Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Research-seed Evidence through: 2026-07-02; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: SUSS MicroTec mainly makes money from advanced-backend bonding equipment, especially temporary bonding / debonding and hybrid bonding. Its AI relevance comes from HBM and AI chip modules raising demand for those backend steps, but that logic still needs to be re-underwritten at a finer customer, product, and economics level.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: SMHN primary-owns the temporary bonding / debonding / hybrid bonding equipment node inside Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. It is not an OSAT capacity platform, not analytics software, and not a test-interface platform; it expresses a narrower and more process-specific advanced-backend step.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If HBM and AI chip modules keep scaling, wafer thinning, temporary bonding / debonding, and die-to-wafer hybrid bonding demand should expand with backend process intensity. SUSS's current revenue bridge first shows up in order intake, order book, and Advanced Backend Solutions scale rather than in separately disclosed AI / HBM revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 order intake reached EUR 149.3m, up 69.5% YoY; SUSS explicitly said the driver was higher demand from key customers for solutions used in the value chain for AI chip modules.
  • Q1 2026 sales were EUR 86.5m, gross margin was 36.1%, EBIT margin was 4.3%, and the order book increased to EUR 330.1m from EUR 266.8m at 2025 year-end.
  • FY2025 sales were EUR 503.2m; Advanced Backend Solutions revenue was EUR 349.7m, up 10.7%.
  • XBC300 Gen2 D2W is described as a fully automated solution for sequential die-to-wafer hybrid bonding on 200mm and 300mm substrates.
  • The 2023 HBM / AI temporary-bonding release explicitly said AI chips combine logic with HBM, that temporary bonding / debonding is indispensable for HBM thinning and downstream processing, and that SUSS temporary bonding is used by one of the world's leading foundries in advanced packaging.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• 2026 guidance points to a slight sales decline and a lower EBIT margin; that is forward-looking management guidance rather than delivered evidence.
  • “Key customers,” “leading foundry,” and the AI-chip-module value-chain wording are issuer statements and should not be upgraded into named-customer monetization proof.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: SUSS is a narrow expression of an advanced-backend equipment step and proves that bonding / debonding / hybrid bonding is not just a story. But the page still carries a re-underwrite modifier because “AI chip modules demand” is not yet the same thing as durable, separable AI / HBM monetization.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Named AI / HBM customers are not disclosed, and AI / HBM revenue mix is not separately disclosed.
  • Advanced Backend Solutions is not the same thing as total advanced-packaging / hybrid-bonding economics.
  • The proof that still needs re-underwriting is customer concentration, the real order mix tied to hybrid bonding / temporary bonding, the conversion of order book into profit, and whether demand persists beyond a single program cycle.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• The AI chip module demand wording disappears or order growth resets sharply.
  • Advanced Backend Solutions keeps scaling without comparable improvement in profit quality or moat.
  • Hybrid bonding / temporary bonding remains demo-scale or overly dependent on one customer.
  • Weak guidance turns out to be structural rather than timing-related.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: SMHN is an Active / Research-seed advanced-backend equipment name with a re-underwrite workflow modifier. To move it higher, the advanced-packaging proof needs to be rebuilt at the named-customer, product, mix, and margin-conversion level rather than staying at order-language plus broad backend scale.

docs.title: SMTC Semtech
docs.text: Role: spine 4 optical/copper Signal Integrity modifier Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Modifier: former-half-hidden Evidence through: 2026-08-25

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Semtech earns from Signal Integrity, Analog Mixed Signal and Wireless, and IoT Systems and Connectivity. Its AI relevance is concentrated in Signal Integrity optical/copper interconnect, while the broader company remains a mixed analog and connectivity platform.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: SMTC primary-owns the high-speed signal-integrity node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI. It is not a module OEM or systems vendor, and its mixed-signal, wireless, and IoT businesses sit outside this page’s primary lane; those edges belong in cross-links such as Semiconductors and Foundational Compute.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If data-center customers buy CopperEdge, FiberEdge, DirectEdge, CDRs, TIAs, drivers, and equalizers, the economics first appear in the Signal Integrity segment. Whether that becomes high-quality AI revenue depends on segment growth, margin, customer proof, and product attribution, not just “800G / 1.6T / 3.2T” marketing language.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• FY2026 Signal Integrity net sales were USD 322.608M, up about 23% from FY2025 USD 261.747M and about 82% above FY2024 USD 177.033M.
  • FY2026 Signal Integrity gross margin was 65.2%; Q4 FY2026 Signal Integrity net sales were USD 90.7M with 67.4% segment gross margin.
  • In the quarter ended 2026-04-26, Signal Integrity net sales were USD 102.003M with 62.7% segment gross margin.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Official materials describe Signal Integrity as an optical/copper data-communications portfolio and position advanced CDRs, copper equalizers, optical solutions, CopperEdge, FiberEdge, and DirectEdge for 800G/1.6T and future use cases; these remain product-positioning claims.
  • Management positions Semtech for the 800G, 1.6T, and 3.2T buildout and says it continues to invest in next-generation optical and copper interconnect technologies.
  • Product pages and press releases frame the 224Gbps family, CopperEdge, FiberEdge, and DirectEdge for AI/ML clusters, hyperscale data centers, cloud infrastructure, and LRO/LPO/XPO/NPO/CPO use cases.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If Signal Integrity keeps outgrowing the rest of the company, Semtech can keep rerating as a data-center interconnect modifier rather than only a mixed analog / IoT name.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Named hyperscaler or NVIDIA revenue is not proven.
  • Named module-vendor volume awards are not proven.
  • CopperEdge / FiberEdge revenue split or a quantified multi-customer production ramp is not proven.
  • A product roadmap does not by itself prove durable high-quality AI revenue.

docs.title: 2026-08-25 Q2 FY2027 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q2 net sales were USD 341.9M, non-GAAP EPS USD 0.71, and operating cash flow/free cash flow USD 68.9M/61.4M.
  • Signal Integrity net sales were USD 126.2M and segment gross margin 65.3%. Q3 guidance was net sales of USD 410M +/- USD 5M and adjusted EPS of USD 1.05 +/- USD 0.03.
  • The release reports accelerating bookings and record backlog but does not quantify CopperEdge, FiberEdge, DirectEdge, customer/module-vendor awards, or hyperscaler revenue. The GAAP net-income line includes a USD 101.4M tax benefit.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• CopperEdge disclosure / litigation risk worsens.
  • Signal Integrity growth or margin weakens materially and stops proving segment importance.
  • The company cannot quantify any durable AI / data-center revenue bridge or customer adoption.
  • Competitors suppress Semtech’s share in the same interconnect / signal-chain budget.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
SMTC is a positive partial proof Signal Integrity modifier. Q2 strengthens segment revenue, margin, and guidance evidence while customer/product revenue attribution, litigation/control-risk detail, and official Q&A remain open.

Current action is routed only by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; SMTC is currently none, with no fallback.

docs.title: SNDK — Sandisk
docs.text: Role: spine 3 data-center flash / NAND storage Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-05

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Sandisk earns from NAND flash, data-center/enterprise storage, and consumer/edge products, relying on its manufacturing JV with Kioxia. AI data growth raises demand for higher-value flash, while NAND pricing, customer commitments, and manufacturing economics remain cyclical.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: SNDK is the data-center flash/capacity-performance node in Memory, Storage, and In-System Data Movement. It differs from MU HBM/DRAM, WDC capacity HDD, and RMBS interface/IP. Enterprise data/context platforms such as SNOW are not physical storage.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Training/inference data, checkpoints, and high-performance datasets raise data-center flash volume and mix, monetized through products and multi-year commitments. NAND ASP, cost per bit, contract pricing/guarantees, concentration, and JV capex determine profit.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q3 FY2026 revenue was USD 5.95B, up 97% sequentially and 251% year over year.
  • Data-center revenue was USD 1.467B, up 233% sequentially and 645% year over year.
  • Sandisk ended Q3 with three signed New Business Model agreements and signed two more in Q4.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: The company calls this a fundamental inflection and describes firm financial commitments in multi-year engagements. Prior Q4 revenue guidance of USD 7.75-8.25B is superseded by the August 5 Q4 actual results above; contract quality, pricing and cash conversion remain research questions.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Higher data-center mix and multi-year contracts may reduce spot-NAND volatility without eliminating supply/pricing cycles.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Backlog/guarantee figures from a third-party transcript are not verified by the local issuer capture and are not treated as facts. Signed agreements do not automatically prove high margin, low concentration, or non-cancellability.

docs.title: 2026-08-05 Q4 FY2026 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q4 revenue was USD 8.97B, up 51% sequentially. FY2026 revenue was USD 20.25B, up 175% year over year, and Datacenter revenue grew 437%.
  • The board approved an additional USD 14B buyback, leaving USD 15.5B authorized. Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance was USD 10.30B-10.80B and non-GAAP EPS guidance USD 44-46.
  • NAND pricing, New Business Model contract quality, customer concentration, and cycle durability remain open.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Data-center revenue/contract conversion slows or concentration and renegotiation rise.
  • NAND supply expansion and falling ASP erode gross margin.
  • JV capex, yield, or technology transitions weaken cash and cost position.
  • Strong guidance fails to become FCF and durable per-share earnings.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
SNDK is an Active / Market-found data-center-flash entity, beyond the old “only NAND cycle/spin” label but still constrained by cycle and contract quality.

docs.title: SNOW — Snowflake
docs.text: Role: E9 data-plane governed cloud data / AI platform owner Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence as of: 2026-05-27; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Snowflake is a governed cloud data platform for enterprise data and AI workloads. Its stable ownership sits at the unified layer for storage, governance, sharing, analytics, and AI capability access, not at the application-owner layer and not in hardware, systems, or physical infrastructure.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: SNOW sits in the E9 data plane across Platform Technology, Internet, and Distribution and AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle. It owns the Data Cloud, Cortex, Snowflake Intelligence, and the consumption platform around enterprise data governance, but it does not absorb application owners, cloud hardware, E2 silicon, E6 systems, or E7/E8 physical infrastructure.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Snowflake's AI-related revenue does not come from a broad AI company narrative. It comes from product consumption on top of the existing data platform: customers keep, govern, and operate data inside Snowflake, then call storage, compute, sharing, Cortex, and AI capabilities. The real proof is whether workload usage, retention, RPO, and AI-capability adoption remain durable.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2027 product revenue was USD 1.33B, up 34% year over year; total revenue was USD 1.39B, up 33%.
  • RPO was USD 9.21B, up 38%; NRR was 126%.
  • Customers with trailing-twelve-month product revenue above USD 1M reached 779, up 29%.
  • More than 13,600 accounts were using Snowflake AI capabilities; Snowflake Intelligence accounts more than doubled quarter over quarter; Cortex Code accounts reached 7,100+.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management continues to frame Snowflake as an AI Data Cloud and raised FY2027 product-revenue guidance to USD 5.84B.
  • Guidance shows demand and management expectation, not already realized AI revenue.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Broad company totals are not AI proof, and AI-capability account counts are not the same as durable monetization.
  • The current local raw corpus does not let this page split every dollar of growth into Cortex, Snowflake Intelligence, or specific agentic-workflow revenue streams.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Snowflake's scarcity comes from enterprise data governance, cross-cloud sharing, and keeping analytics plus AI usage inside one governed platform. The misread boundary is turning it into an application owner, a generic software seat story, or a hardware / physical-buildout owner. It owns the data plane, not the endpoints or the physical stack.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If retention, RPO, million-dollar customers, and AI-capability adoption start diverging, the data-plane monetization case needs to be re-underwritten.
  • If AI capabilities remain enablement without sustained product consumption, the thesis strength is overstated.
  • If later local source work no longer supports the governed cloud data / AI platform role, this page should contract.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: SNOW is Core / Market-found. Its stable E9 ownership is the governed cloud data / AI platform and does not extend into application owners, E2 silicon, E6 systems, or E7/E8 physical infrastructure. Any current action lives only in Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger.

docs.title: SOFI — SoFi Technologies
docs.text: Role: E10 cross-theme digital-bank, lending, and financial-services platform Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Updated: 2026-07-13; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: SoFi combines a member entry point, lending, financial-services products, and the external-client Galileo technology platform. Core revenue still comes from spread, fees, and platform/service economics rather than a standalone AI revenue line.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: SOFI belongs to the E10 cross-theme fintech portfolio, not a tenth AI or data-center supply spine. It owns the digital-bank, lending, and financial-services-platform role. It does not absorb HOOD's retail-brokerage and crypto entry point, AFRM's BNPL merchant network, or a generic application or physical-infrastructure role.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI is currently a support layer inside loan-application workflow and service productivity. If it improves underwriting, document handling, service efficiency, or user experience, value must still show up through conversion, credit outcomes, cost efficiency, spread, fees, or platform revenue. AI is not separately disclosed as revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Official IR materials and the Q1 FY2026 8-K describe SoFi as a member-centric one-stop digital financial-services platform with lending, financial-services, and technology-platform segments.
  • The Q1 FY2026 packet records member/product, origination, loan-platform, lending net-interest-income, and brokerage-fee anchors. These are broad financial-services actuals, not AI-attributed revenue.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company describes Personal Loan Doc Coach as an AI-powered tool inside the loan-application workflow.
  • That product framing proves AI has entered the service workflow, not standalone AI monetization.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI-assisted workflow shortens application and service cycles and improves underwriting consistency, SoFi may benefit through conversion, cost, and credit outcomes.
  • Wider external Galileo use could add platform revenue that differs from balance-sheet spread economics.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AI has created separately trackable revenue, ARR, or profit contribution.
  • Broad member, product, origination, or lending growth is directly attributable to AI.
  • SOFI should absorb HOOD, AFRM, or a wider application or infrastructure-owner role.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If credit performance or funding costs deteriorate, member and origination growth may not become durable earnings.
  • If external Galileo growth stalls, SoFi will remain more dependent on balance-sheet spread and the consumer-credit cycle.
  • If AI tools produce no verifiable conversion, cost, credit, or paid result, this page should keep AI as a support layer.

docs.title: TER — Teradyne
docs.text: Role: spine 5 manufacturing / packaging / test / materials context; ATE benchmark-only Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-02-10; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Teradyne makes money from semiconductor test platforms. Its AI relevance is real because HBM, chiplets, and 2.5D / 3D packages increase memory-test, thermal-aware-test, and known-good-everything complexity, but it is still a broad ATE platform rather than an advanced-packaging owner.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: TER is only a test-infrastructure benchmark inside Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. It does not own the packaging-equipment node or the materials / purity node; this page exists to benchmark narrower names such as FORM, SMHN, and PDFS rather than to promote TER as the primary execution name.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As AI chips move from monolithic die to chiplets, HBM, and larger advanced packages, testing expands beyond a single die toward die, bridge, interposer, substrate, and stack validation. Teradyne's revenue bridge comes from higher memory / compute test intensity, not from packaging capacity itself.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q4 2025 results were above the high end of guidance, and management explicitly said growth was fueled by AI-related demand in compute, networking, and memory within Semi Test.
  • Teradyne's technical article explicitly said the industry has entered the era of heterogeneous chiplets in advanced integrated packages, where AI packages combine CPUs, GPUs, and HBM in a single advanced package.
  • The same article directly connected CoWoS, 2.5D / 3D packaging, large CoW modules, thermal dissipation, and rising test complexity.
  • The article also extended the test problem from known-good-die to known-good-interposer and known-good-CoW style validation.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 guidance was revenue of USD 1.15B-1.25B; that remains forward-looking guidance rather than delivered evidence.
  • Management expects year-over-year growth across all businesses in 2026, with strong momentum in compute driven by AI; that is forward-looking outlook rather than a proven revenue split.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: TER proves that AI / HBM / chiplet complexity raises the value of test infrastructure, but it is best used as a benchmark-only ATE platform. Writing it as the owner of the advanced-packaging lane would blur platform test exposure with packaging-node ownership.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• HBM-related test revenue is not separately disclosed.
  • The advanced-packaging share of revenue is not separately disclosed.
  • It is not proven that TER should primary-own the spine 5 packaging lane.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI stops showing up as a direct Semi Test demand driver.
  • Higher test complexity fails to translate into better business quality or higher value capture.
  • TER trades more like undifferentiated broad ATE beta and loses its usefulness as a benchmark reference.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: TER is a Context / Market-found ATE benchmark-only name. It stays in the wiki to calibrate the upper bound and maturity of the test layer, not to be upgraded into the primary advanced-packaging execution name.

docs.title: TLN — Talen Energy
docs.text:
Role: Phase 5 E7 spine 7 generation / grid / time-to-power; TLN owns dispatchable generation and campus power contracting Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-05

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects VST, CEG, and TLN Current Live Research Conclusion as TLN's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Talen is an independent power producer centered on PJM. It owns Susquehanna nuclear generation plus gas and other dispatchable assets, and it earns through wholesale energy, capacity, ancillary services, and long-term power contracts.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Within Power Generation, Grid, and Fuel Supply, TLN primary-owns dispatchable generation and campus power contracting. It owns site-level generation, PJM energy/capacity monetization, and campus-power contracts such as AWS. Its ownership stops at the site / utility handoff; inside-the-fence switchgear, UPS, cooling, and server / network layers do not belong here.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: TLN's cleanest AI monetization path is to bind Susquehanna's nuclear output to long-duration contracts for an adjacent data-center campus, then use PJM dispatchable assets and added capacity to backstop delivery. The monetized layer is site-level electricity, capacity, and contractual delivery, not data-center internal infrastructure.

docs.title: 2026-08-05 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was USD 374M and adjusted free cash flow was USD 212M.
  • The company raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to USD 2.025B-2.225B and adjusted free-cash-flow guidance to USD 1.200B-1.350B. These guide figures do not make total generation earnings AI-specific.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The 2025 annual report disclosed about 13.1 GW of power infrastructure, including about 2.2 GW of nuclear generation, plus a meaningful dispatchable fossil fleet.

  • The Q1 2026 10-Q disclosed that the revised AWS PPA moved to a front-of-the-meter structure providing up to 1,920 MW through 2042; the transition to the revised structure occurred in April 2026.

  • The August 5 Q2 release confirms that Cornerstone closed in June 2026, adding about 2.6GW of generation, and cites a pipeline of about 4GW of land-development and data-center contracting options.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The earlier Q1 full-year Adjusted EBITDA / Adjusted FCF guidance explicitly excluded Cornerstone. That is a historical pre-close basis and cannot automatically be applied to the raised August 5 guidance above.
  • Q1 2026 results and the April 2026 senior-notes release disclosed Cornerstone assets of Lawrenceburg 1,120 MW, Waterford 875 MW, and Darby 456 MW, or 2,451 MW total; these are pre-close asset/financing disclosures; the Q2 release confirms that closing occurred in June 2026.
  • The shareholder letter describes the expanded AWS PPA as roughly USD 18B of 17-year notional revenues and treats it as a base for further data-center contracting.
  • Management frames Freedom, Guernsey, and the Cornerstone assets as part of the Flywheel strategy to strengthen future campus / large-load contracting capability.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• TLN is one of the clearest cases of a single nuclear campus directly tied to AI power demand, which makes the ownership very pure but also concentrates the risk in Susquehanna, AWS, and PJM / FERC rules.
  • Added and acquired gas assets make TLN look more like a dispatchable platform that can backstop long-duration contracts, rather than only a single nuclear-asset story.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The full AWS ramp schedule, post-close Cornerstone integration and economics, and TLN's ability to expand campus-power contracting beyond Susquehanna / AWS are not yet proven by reported results.
  • TLN's total PJM revenue base or total generation earnings should not be treated as equivalent to AI monetization.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• The AWS PPA's regulatory or contractual path is materially weakened, or the front-of-the-meter structure cannot advance as disclosed.
  • Susquehanna availability, licensing support, or safety / operating performance materially weaken long-duration delivery capability.
  • PJM / FERC large-load or co-location rule changes materially damage campus-power contracting economics.
  • Post-close Cornerstone integration or economics disappoint in a way that weakens TLN's dispatchable backstop and contracting capacity.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: TLN is the Core / Market-found dispatchable generation and campus power contracting owner on the generation spine. The ownership stops at the power site and grid delivery layer, not the campus mechanical/electrical or IT stack.

docs.text: Last updated: 2026-04-16 02:45 CEST Industry page: Platform Technology, Internet, and Distribution Classification: conditional

docs.title: Theme position
docs.text: Consumer technology endpoint, vehicle software, autonomous driving / Robotaxi, energy storage, and robotics optionality.

docs.title: Why it belongs in this theme
docs.text: Its core business remains vehicles and energy storage, but official filings have already positioned FSD, Robotaxi, Optimus, Cortex, and energy software as core technology pathways, so I view it as best monitored under conditional classification.

docs.title: My currently more credible bullish case
docs.text: Energy storage is becoming a second growth leg, and if autonomy and Robotaxi deliver, Tesla can move from a manufacturing story toward a software/platform valuation framework.

docs.title: My current top risks
docs.text: Automotive margins and delivery cadence still determine current cash flow; misalignment between autonomous-driving timelines, regulation, and valuation expectations can be very painful.

docs.title: One-line view
docs.text: In this conditional lens, the core business is still vehicles and storage, but autonomous driving and robotics optionality justify keeping it in the platform-technology watchlist.
